Ghar.tv · Build with what exists

Components

Every part of the portal you can pick up and put on a page. Each preview runs on the production CSS and JS, and its code is one click away. For when and why to use something, see the Design System.

  • 137components
  • 119paste
  • 14include
  • 4call

Paste

Copy the HTML into your page and load the files listed under Needs. If it is marked Inline CSS, paste its CSS tab into the page too.

Include

Shared chrome like the nav and footer. Never paste it. Add the PARTIAL marker, set the body classes, then run npm run build:partials. A pasted copy is overwritten on the next build.

Call

A function in a shared script. Load the script and call it. There is no markup to paste, and no second copy of the logic to write.

For AI tools

Read COMPONENTS.md, a small index. Pick one, then read only its source file. components.json holds everything in one file. Copy for AI on any component gives a ready brief.

Foundations

Section typography

Paste In shared CSS

The three text roles every section header is built from: a tracked-caps Inter eyebrow, a Gazpacho Bold display title with size steps, and an Inter lead paragraph. The head layouts arrange them; these classes paint them.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 3 pages

brands.html index.html people.html

Guidelines
An older trio still ships on the B2B pages and index.html's .sec-hdr: .eyebrow (600 weight, 0.1em, --faint), .display (Gazpacho with letter-spacing -.025em, against the no-negative-tracking rule) and .lead (--muted, 1.82). CLAUDE.md describes the eyebrow with the older values. New work uses the .sec-* classes.
Preview 
<span class="sec-eyebrow">Eyebrow</span>
<h2 class="sec-title">A short title that owns its line.</h2>
<p class="sec-lead">One or two sentences that set up the section for the reader.</p>

Use it when

  • .sec-eyebrow for the short category label above a title
  • .sec-title for the section's display heading; --md for sub-section heads, --sub for the related and more-from modules under an article, --sm for a compact tracked-caps title
  • .sec-lead for the one or two sentences that set a section up

Avoid

  • A section-prefixed copy of these (.intl4-eyebrow, .gt4-title). They were removed; co-class instead
  • Red on the eyebrow. Eyebrows stay muted
  • Negative letter-spacing or italics on Gazpacho
  • Shrinking a title to fit long copy. Give it width (.sec-title--wide) rather than smaller type

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.sec-eyebrowclassInter 700 10px, 0.14em tracking, uppercase, --muted.
.sec-titleclassGazpacho 700, clamp(34px, 4.4vw, 56px), line-height 1.08, ink, no margin.
.sec-title--mdmodifierclamp(26px, 2.6vw, 38px), line-height 1.12.
.sec-title--submodifierclamp(22px, 1.9vw, 26px), for navigation modules below an article.
.sec-title--smmodifierSwitches to Inter 700 11px tracked caps.
.sec-leadclassInter 15px, line-height 1.75, --espresso.

Source _dev/reference/components/type-section.html

Buttons & links

Button

Paste In shared CSS

The general-purpose .btn chassis for page actions that are not the section CTA: load more, a strip's view-all, a contribute panel's two actions. One base class for geometry, one modifier for the colour role.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 19 pages

brand-partners.html brands-search.html brands.html brokers.html buyers.html design-architecture.html design-heritage.html design-series.html developers.html for-brands.html ghartalks-article.html ghartalks-category.html ghartalks.html index.html people-search.html people.html voices-conversations.html voices-search.html voices.html

Guidelines
.btn.btn-primary paints almost exactly what .btn-text paints (ink outline, 10px radius, ink fill on hover). The two grew separately; .btn-text is the one reserved for section heads. brokers, buyers, developers, brand-partners and for-brands define their own .btn, .btn-p, .btn-s and .btn-ghost inline, so on those pages the shared chassis is overridden.
Preview 
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">
  Load more stories
  <svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12l7 7 7-7"/></svg>
</button>

<a href="/path" class="btn btn-accent">Primary panel action</a>

<!-- On a dark ground -->
<a href="/path" class="btn btn-ghost">Action on dark</a>

Use it when

  • .btn.btn-primary for a quiet, outlined page action: Load more, All stories in a tag strip
  • .btn.btn-accent for the one dark, filled action of a panel, such as Pitch a conversation or Download media kit
  • .btn.btn-ghost when the button sits on a dark ground and needs a translucent white outline

Avoid

  • The section header CTA. That is .btn-text, one per section
  • A CTA inside a card. Cards use the card link (.btn-link) or link as a whole
  • Red fills. Red is reserved for page-level brand actions such as Post Property
  • Pairing .btn-accent with .btn-primary side by side: on hover the outline fills with ink and both buttons turn dark. Use the paired CTA instead
  • Redefining .btn or .btn-ghost in a page <style> block. Some B2B pages do, and the local rule silently overrides the shared one

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.btnclassGeometry only: inline-flex, 13px Inter 600, 13px 24px padding, 10px radius, 1.5px border, 1px press on :active, ink focus ring.
.btn-primarymodifierInk outline on transparent. Fills with ink and turns the label white on hover.
.btn-accentmodifierInk fill, white label. Hover lightens to #1f1f1f.
.btn-ghostmodifierFor dark grounds: 18% white outline, 80% white label, brightens on hover.
.btn-quietmodifierEspresso rule on warm white, fills espresso on hover. Defined in shared CSS, not used on any page yet.
svgslotOptional trailing icon. .btn does not size it, so give the svg width and height attributes or a page rule.

Source _dev/reference/components/button.html

Card link

Paste In shared CSS

The text plus arrow cue that sits inside a card: no border, no fill, 13px ink. On hover the gap widens and the arrow slides; the colour never changes.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 8 pages

design-architecture.html ghartalks-category.html ghartalks.html index.html voices-article.html voices-conversations.html voices-speakers.html voices.html

Guidelines
Rule 03 in design-system.html (#cr-cta) still says the card link turns brand red on hover. Production CSS and the house rule both keep it ink; follow production.
Preview 
<!-- Inside a whole-card link: a span, never a nested <a> -->
<a href="/path">
  <!-- card content -->
  <span class="btn-link">
    Explore finance
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
  </span>
</a>

<!-- Standalone, underlined -->
<a href="/path" class="btn-link btn-link--underline">
  Read the conversation
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
</a>

Use it when

  • The inner cue of a whole-card link, as a <span> inside the card's <a> (Explore finance)
  • A standalone read link in a quiet context, with .btn-link--underline, when nothing else on the block says link
  • The last line of a card body, with .btn-link--gap-top so it clears the description

Avoid

  • The section's main CTA. That is .btn-text in the section head
  • A pill or bordered button inside a card: it competes with the section CTA
  • A red hover. Text links stay ink and motion is the only hover cue
  • An <a> nested inside a card that is already an <a>. Use a <span class="btn-link"> there

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.btn-linkclassInline-flex text + arrow, 13px Inter 600 ink, no wrap. Hover widens the gap 6px to 9px and slides the svg 2px.
.btn-link--underlinemodifier1px underline at 4px offset, thickens to 2px on hover. For a block with no other link chrome.
.btn-link--gap-topmodifierAdds 6px top margin so the cue clears the description above it.
svgslotTrailing arrow, sized 12px by the class. Keep aria-hidden.

Source _dev/reference/components/button-card-link.html

Inline links

Paste In shared CSS

Two small text-link atoms for meta rows and quiet footers of a block: a faint muted link that brightens to ink, and the red arrow link that is one of the few sanctioned red text uses.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 1 page

index.html

Guidelines
.arrow-link has shared CSS but no root page uses it today; only .muted-link ships (index.html). Modal legal links (.jm-link a, .jm-terms a) belong to the form system.
Preview 
<a href="/path" class="muted-link">View all episodes</a>

<a href="/path" class="arrow-link">
  See methodology
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
</a>

Use it when

  • .muted-link for a secondary or meta link beside a main action (a deck download next to a media kit button)
  • .arrow-link for a single See more affordance where red is earned

Avoid

  • Re-authoring a link style per section. Copy these classes
  • .arrow-link more than once in a view: red stays near 5% of the page
  • Either one as a section CTA (.btn-text) or a card cue (.btn-link)
  • A red hover on any other text link

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.muted-linkclass13px Inter 500 in --faint, no underline, turns ink on hover. Dark sections (#gharEvents, #videoWorks, #ecosystem) repaint it translucent white.
.arrow-linkclass13px Inter 600 in --red with a trailing arrow. Gap widens 5px to 9px and the svg slides 2px on hover.
svgslotArrow inside .arrow-link, sized 14px by the class.

Source _dev/reference/components/link-inline.html

Paired CTA

Paste In shared CSS

The canonical treatment whenever two buttons sit side by side: the main action dark, the secondary a quiet white that only warms on hover. The hierarchy survives the hover state.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
WhereNot on a shipped page yetGuidelines
Same markup as the actions row in form-structure; this entry exists so the pairing rule can be found from Buttons. No root page renders .jm-actions directly: person profiles copy these colour values into their own .pp-btn pair. ghartalks.html pairs .btn.btn-accent with .btn.btn-primary in its pitch panel, and the outline inverts to ink on hover, which is the mistake this pattern exists to prevent.
Preview 
<div class="jm-actions">
  <button type="button" class="jm-btn jm-btn--secondary">Cancel</button>
  <button type="submit" class="jm-btn jm-btn--primary">Send brief</button>
</div>

Use it when

  • Any two actions on one line: Cancel and Confirm in a modal, Back and Continue in a form step
  • As the colour source for inline page pairs with their own geometry (the person profile hero pair takes its colours from here)

Avoid

  • A transparent secondary that inverts to ink on hover. Two dark buttons side by side lose the hierarchy
  • Two primaries. One view, one committed action
  • Putting the primary on the left. The secondary sits left so the primary keeps the rightmost position
  • Changing the colours when the geometry has to change. Geometry may be local, colour may not

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-actionsclassFlex row, 12px gap. Removes the stacked margin from each button inside it.
.jm-btnclassForm-system button geometry: full width of its cell, 16px padding, 14px radius, 15px Inter 600, scale(.98) on press.
.jm-btn--primarymodifierInk fill, white label. Hover #222 plus a soft shadow. Greys out when disabled.
.jm-btn--secondarymodifierWhite fill, ink label, hairline field-rule border. Hover: warm-white fill and ink border, never dark.

Source _dev/reference/components/button-pair.html

Layout

3-column editorial grid

Paste In shared CSS

A supporting left column, a prominent centre column and a supporting right column. On phones the columns stack; between 576px and 1079px the centre spans the top with the sides paired below; from 1080px it is three columns with hairline dividers around the centre.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 2 pages

design-architecture.html design.html

Guidelines
The /design hero co-classes this with its old .hero-v2__split / __col-l / __col-c / __col-r names, which still carry page-level rules.
Preview 
<div class="grid-3col-editorial">
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col">
    <!-- left supporting items -->
  </div>
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col grid-3col-editorial__col--center">
    <!-- the lead item -->
  </div>
  <div class="grid-3col-editorial__col">
    <!-- right supporting items -->
  </div>
</div>

Use it when

  • An editorial roundup or hero where one story leads and two columns of lighter items flank it (the /design hero and Inspiration roundup)
  • .grid-3col-editorial--center-first when the centre column must come first on a phone even though it sits in the middle of the DOM

Avoid

  • Three equal cards. That is a plain 24px-gap grid, not an editorial hierarchy
  • Turning the side columns into a carousel below 1080px. The tablet layout is the shared rule; forking it to a rail is what this replaced
  • Reordering columns in page CSS. Use the modifier

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.grid-3col-editorialclassThe grid. 1fr on phones, 2-up with a spanning centre from 576px, 1fr 1.6fr 1fr from 1080px, 1fr 2fr 1fr from 1280px.
.grid-3col-editorial__colclassA column: flex column with a 48px gap (56px from 1080px), min-width 0.
.grid-3col-editorial__col--centermodifierThe prominent column. Spans the top row on tablet; 24px side padding and hairline borders on desktop.
.grid-3col-editorial--center-firstmodifierOrders the centre first when stacked. Defined in shared CSS, not used on a page yet.

Source _dev/reference/components/grid-3col-editorial.html

Panel bleed

Paste In shared CSS

A contained, rounded content panel that becomes a full-width band below 1024px, so its content lands on the same gutter as every other section instead of being indented twice on a phone.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 1 page

videoworks.html

Guidelines
Only /videoworks uses it today, on .vw-sec__inner panels styled in videoworks.css.
Preview 
<div class="my-panel panel-bleed">
  <!-- the block of content -->
</div>

Use it when

  • A tinted or bordered panel inside a section that holds a whole block: a process grid, an FAQ, a stat table
  • Any panel where the rounded box is presentation rather than meaning

Avoid

  • A small card, a callout, or one item among several. Those should read as discrete objects, not stretch to the viewport
  • A whole <section> that should run edge to edge. That is section.section--bleed
  • Styling the panel's border-radius or padding outside a min-width: 1024px query. A plain page rule outranks this single class and the bleed half-applies
  • Escalating the utility with !important to win that fight

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.panel-bleedclassBelow 1024px: negative --pad-h inline margin, equal inline padding, no radius, no side borders. No effect from 1024px.
page ruleslotThe page owns background, border-block and padding-block at every width, and states its contained look (border, radius, padding-inline) only inside @media (min-width: 1024px).

Source _dev/reference/components/panel-bleed.html

Section head (horizontal)

Paste In shared CSS

Eyebrow and display title on the left, a text plus arrow See all link on the right, baseline-aligned in one flex row. The compact variant turns the title into a small tracked-caps label for sub-clusters.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 6 pages

brands.html design-architecture.html design-article.html design.html people.html voices-article.html

Guidelines
Preview 
<!-- Main -->
<div class="section-head">
  <div class="section-head__text">
    <span class="sec-eyebrow">Eyebrow</span>
    <h2 class="sec-title sec-title--md">Section title</h2>
  </div>
  <a class="section-head__link" href="/path">
    See all
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
  </a>
</div>

<!-- Compact sub-cluster -->
<div class="section-head section-head--compact">
  <h2 class="sec-title sec-title--sm">Designers</h2>
  <a href="/design/designers" class="section-head__link">
    See all designers
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
  </a>
</div>

Use it when

  • Directory and pillar pages (/design, /brands, /people) that open a block with a title and a See all
  • .section-head--compact for quiet sub-cluster heads above a rail: Designers, Brands, In focus
  • .section-head__link when a bordered .btn-text would be too heavy for the head

Avoid

  • Homepage storytelling sections with a lead paragraph. Those use the split head (.sec-head), with the .btn-text CTA under the lead
  • Confusing .section-head with .sec-head. The names are nearly identical but the layouts are not: .sec-head stacks, .section-head is one row
  • A per-section head class (.cl-head, .nr-head, .gt4-head). Nineteen of those were collapsed into this
  • Putting the See all in the foot row under a carousel. The foot row is for arrows and dots

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.section-headclassFlex row, space-between, align-items flex-end, wraps. clamp(32px, 4vw, 48px) bottom margin.
.section-head__textclassColumn for eyebrow + title, 10px gap, min-width 0.
.section-head__linkclass13px Inter 600 ink link with a 14px arrow. Gap and arrow move on hover. Works on <a> or on a <button> that opens a dialog.
.section-head--compactmodifierBaseline-aligned, 40px bottom margin (28px when followed by .rail-outer). On phones title and link stay on one row.
.sec-title--smmodifierThe compact title: Inter 700 11px tracked caps in ink.
.sec-title--mdmodifierMid-size Gazpacho title, clamp(26px, 2.6vw, 38px).

Source _dev/reference/components/section-head.html

Only index.html uses this head today, and several sections still carry a leftover prefix class beside it (.intl4-head, .gt4-head-l). The design-system Rule 02 mock names the wrapper .section-inner, which exists on no page; the real inner container is .section-wrap.

<div class="sec-head">

  • Homepage and vertical-landing sections that set up their content with a lead paragraph and one CTA (Intelligence, GharTalks, For Brokers)
  • .sec-title--narrow (16ch) or .sec-title--wide (18ch) so a long title breaks early beside the lead on desktop
  • .sec-head-r--tight when the lead is short and the CTA should sit closer to it
  • .section-pills-strip on the category strip directly under the head, so the gap to the carousel is the standard one

Avoid

  • Putting the CTA in the foot row under the carousel. It goes under the lead
  • More than one CTA in the head, or a .btn-link there. The section CTA is .btn-text
  • Directory or pillar heads with a See all and no lead: use the horizontal .section-head
  • A per-section max-width on the title. Co-class --narrow or --wide instead
  • A new one-property class for the strip's margin (.X-chips-outer). Co-class .section-pills-strip

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.sec-headclassColumn flex, 18px gap, clamp(28px, 3vw, 40px) bottom margin.
.sec-head-rowclassStacks below 1024px; from 1024px a space-between row with a 48px gap.
.sec-head-lclassTitle column, flexes and can shrink.
.sec-head-rclassLead + CTA column, 22px gap, capped at 420px on desktop.
.sec-head-r--tightmodifier18px gap between lead and CTA.
.sec-title--narrowmodifiermax-width 16ch from 1024px. No cap on mobile.
.sec-title--widemodifiermax-width 18ch from 1024px.
.section-pills-stripclassSpacing slot for the tag strip under the head: margin-bottom clamp(28px, 3vw, 40px). --gap-top adds the same above.

Source _dev/reference/components/section-head-split.html

Section wrap and block

Paste In shared CSS

The outer shell of every section. The <section> itself gets its vertical padding from one portal-wide rule; .section-block carries an optional tint band; .section-wrap centres the content at --max-w with the responsive --pad-h gutter.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 5 pages

design-architecture.html design-heritage.html design-series.html design.html index.html

Guidelines
CLAUDE.md still quotes --pad-v as clamp(80px, 9vw, 120px) and the design-system entry says a 1280px floor; styles.css :root is the source that ships. The B2B pages (brokers, buyers, developers, brand-partners, brand-connect) use the older .wrap class, which bakes the vertical padding in.
Preview 
<!-- Plain section -->
<section id="my-section" aria-labelledby="my-section-h">
  <div class="section-wrap">
    <!-- content -->
  </div>
</section>

<!-- Tinted band -->
<section id="my-band" class="section-block section-block--warm" aria-labelledby="my-band-h">
  <div class="section-wrap">
    <!-- content -->
  </div>
</section>

Use it when

  • Every section on every page: a plain <section> directly inside <body>, <main> or .page-wrap already gets padding-block: var(--pad-v)
  • .section-wrap as the inner container, or as a co-class on the section when there is no tint
  • .section-block.section-block--warm when the section needs a warm-white band behind it
  • .section-wrap--bleed for a full-width image section whose children should reach the viewport edge

Avoid

  • A per-section class that re-states max-width, auto margins and padding. That is the duplication this replaced
  • Authoring padding: var(--pad-v) 0 per section. The universal section rule already applies it
  • A section prefix class that sets more than its unique rhythm or tint. Horizontal sizing belongs to .section-wrap
  • Warm white as the default ground. White is the ground; warm is an earned band

API

NameTypeWhat it does
main > sectionslotTop-level sections inside body, main or .page-wrap get padding-block: var(--pad-v) from styles.css.
.section-wrapclassmax-width: var(--max-w), auto side margins, padding-inline: var(--pad-h).
.section-wrap--bleedmodifierDrops the side padding so children reach the edges.
.section-blockclassNo rule of its own any more: its padding moved to the universal section rule. Kept as the base the tint modifiers hang off.
.section-block--warmmodifierbackground: var(--warm-white).
--max-w / --pad-h / --pad-vtoken1600px; clamp(24px, 3vw, 80px); clamp(48px, 5vw, 72px) as defined in styles.css :root.

Load more

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

A single button under a directory grid that reveals the next batch in place. The shared gharGridReveal helper counts whole rows off the live column count, so no batch ever leaves a ragged part-row, and it hides the button when nothing is left.

Needs/dist/styles.min.cssgsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.jsgsap@3.14.2/dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js/dist/main.min.js
Where
Used on 6 pages

brands-search.html brands.html design-heritage.html people-search.html people.html voices-search.html

Guidelines
The sentinel body is copied three times inline: .br-loadmore (brands.html), .pe-loadmore (people.html) and .dp-loadmore (design-heritage.html). A shared .load-more block with a count line exists in styles.css but no page uses it.
Preview 
<div class="my-grid" id="myGrid">
  <!-- all cards, already in the DOM -->
</div>
<div class="br-loadmore" id="myLoadMore" aria-live="polite">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" data-loadmore>
    Load more
    <svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12l7 7 7-7"/></svg>
  </button>
</div>
.br-loadmore{
  display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; align-items:center;
  gap:12px;
  min-height:140px;
  padding:clamp(28px,3vw,44px) 0;
  margin-top:clamp(32px,3vw,48px);
}
.br-loadmore.is-done{display:none}
window.gharGridReveal({
  grid:         document.getElementById('myGrid'),
  sentinel:     document.getElementById('myLoadMore'),
  cardSelector: '.my-card',
  initialRows:  4,
  batchRows:    3,
});

Use it when

  • Directory and archive grids where the reader is grazing: /brands, /people, a pillar tag page
  • Any grid that already holds all its items in the DOM and should show them a few rows at a time

Avoid

  • Infinite scroll. It makes the footer unreachable and hides how much is left
  • Counting a fixed number of cards. The same 12 is 4 rows at 3-up and 12 rows at 1-up; batch in rows
  • A spinner and a Loading label when the items are already on the page. The button reveals, it does not fetch
  • A dead button that stays visible after the last batch. The sentinel takes .is-done and hides
  • Numbered pages here. Use pagination only when a reader needs to return to a known position

API

NameTypeWhat it does
[data-loadmore]attributeMarks the button inside the sentinel. Its presence switches gharGridReveal from scroll-triggered to click-triggered.
.br-loadmoreclassThe sentinel: centred column under the grid, aria-live="polite". Rename the prefix per page only if you must; the body is identical.
.is-donemodifierAdded to the sentinel by the helper when every item is showing; hides it.
gharGridRevealJSgharGridReveal({ grid, sentinel, cardSelector, initialRows, batchRows }). Adds .is-hidden to items past the budget and .is-revealing to a batch as it appears. Exposes grid.__revealAll() and grid.__revealReset() for filters.
.is-hiddenmodifierSet on grid children by the helper. The page must hide it: .my-grid > .is-hidden { display: none }.

Source _dev/reference/components/load-more.html

Use it when

Avoid

  • Editorial browsing where the reader is grazing. Use load more
  • The carousel dot row. That is .dc-paginator

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.pagerclassThe <nav aria-label>: centred wrapping row, 6px gap.
.pager__btnclassA page or arrow control. aria-current="page" marks the current page; aria-disabled="true" greys an unavailable arrow.
.pager__btn--nummodifierA numbered page. Hidden below 744px unless it is the current page.
.pager__gapclassThe ellipsis between number runs, aria-hidden. Hidden on phones.
.pager__countclassFull-width count line under the row, tabular numbers.

Guidelines
Root pages carry it only inside the mobile search modal partial (.seg--choice.seg--ink). The tab form ships in shared CSS and JS with no page using it yet.
Preview 
<!-- Tabs: swaps a panel -->
<div class="seg" role="tablist" aria-label="Listing mode">
  <button type="button" class="seg__btn" role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="panelBuy" id="tabBuy">Buy</button>
  <button type="button" class="seg__btn" role="tab" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1" aria-controls="panelRent" id="tabRent">Rent</button>
</div>
<div id="panelBuy" class="tabs__panel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="tabBuy">...</div>
<div id="panelRent" class="tabs__panel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="tabRent" hidden>...</div>

<!-- Choice: answers a question in a form -->
<div class="seg seg--choice seg--ink" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Buy or rent">
  <button type="button" class="seg__btn" role="radio" aria-checked="true">Buy</button>
  <button type="button" class="seg__btn" role="radio" aria-checked="false" tabindex="-1">Rent</button>
</div>

Use it when

  • role="tablist" with .seg__btn role="tab" to switch a view in place: Buy, Rent, PG
  • .seg.seg--choice.seg--ink as a role="radiogroup" for a question inside a form or search step: Buy or rent, property type
  • .seg--dark on a dark panel

Avoid

  • More than five options. That is a select
  • Filtering a list (use the pills strip) or moving to another page (use the subnav)
  • An .active class. aria-selected (tabs) or aria-checked (choice) is the only state, and the CSS keys off it
  • A per-page click handler. No init call is needed; a second listener is how the two meanings drift apart

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.segclassThe track: inline-flex pill on --bg3, scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping.
.seg__btnclassOne option. Selected state comes from aria-selected="true" or aria-checked="true".
.seg--choicemodifierForm either/or: full width, 44px touch height, segments size to their label, a single thumb slides between them.
.seg--inkmodifierWith --choice: the thumb is ink and the chosen label white.
.seg--darkmodifierTranslucent white track and a white selected pill, for dark grounds.
.seg__icoclassOptional leading icon inside a choice segment.
gharSegFitJSgharSegFit(group) re-measures one .seg--choice thumb. Call it after un-hiding a group that was measured at zero width.
gharSegWatchJSRe-scans the page for .seg--choice groups and observes their size. Runs on DOMContentLoaded.
changeeventA radiogroup option dispatches a bubbling change event from the chosen .seg__btn, by click or arrow key. Tablists emit nothing.
.tabs__panelclassThe panel a tab controls via aria-controls; toggled with the hidden attribute.

<div class="tip tip--below tip--end">
  <button type="button" class="tip__anchor" aria-label="Share this page" aria-describedby="tipShare">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="18" cy="5" r="3"/><circle cx="6" cy="12" r="3"/><circle cx="18" cy="19" r="3"/><line x1="8.59" y1="13.51" x2="15.42" y2="17.49"/><line x1="15.41" y1="6.51" x2="8.59" y2="10.49"/></svg>

Use it when

  • .tip__trigger to gloss a term the reader may not know: carpet area, RERA ID, super built-up
  • .tip__anchor on an existing icon button or link to name it (Share this profile, a website link)
  • .tip--below near the top of the viewport; --start and --end for the first and last control in a row against the screen edge

Avoid

  • Anything required to finish a task. Touch has no hover, so the bubble cannot be the only way to know
  • Help that fits in the interface: a clearer label or a help line under the field comes first
  • More than about twenty-five words for a gloss, or more than two or three words for a name
  • Dropping aria-label on an anchored control. The bubble is invisible to assistive tech; both are needed
  • The hover-expand pill that grows sideways to reveal a label. It moves layout and never opens on touch

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.tipclassPositioning wrapper around the trigger and its bubble.
.tip__triggerclassThe round ? button. Must be a real <button type="button"> with aria-describedby.
.tip__anchorclassAdds no appearance: marks an existing control as the bubble's owner.
.tip__bubbleclassrole="tooltip" with an id, placed immediately after the trigger or anchor. Ink bubble with an arrow, above by default.
.tip--belowmodifierOpens below the control.
.tip--startmodifierAnchors the bubble to the control's left edge.
.tip--endmodifierAnchors the bubble to the control's right edge.

<div id="tpPlans" class="tabs__panel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="tabPlans" hidden>...</div>

Use it when

  • Switching between views of one subject inside a page body, where a pill group would read as a control rather than structure: Overview, Floor plans, Neighbourhood

Avoid

  • Two or three short options in a compact spot. Use the segmented control
  • Filtering a list that stays on screen (pills strip) or linking to other pages (subnav)
  • Hiding content the page's job depends on behind a second tab
  • Wiring your own click handler or an .active class. aria-selected is the state

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.tabsclassThe role="tablist" row. Scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping.
.tabs__btnclassOne role="tab". aria-selected="true" turns it ink and scales its underline in.
.tabs__panelclassrole="tabpanel" named by aria-controls; hidden when not selected.

Source _dev/reference/components/tabs.html

Utility classes

Paste In shared CSS

Single-purpose helper classes for the jobs every card and section repeats: fill a box, crop an image, lock an aspect ratio, clamp or truncate backend text, align numbers, collapse empty fields, and set a brand colour directly on an element.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 1 page

index.html

Guidelines
Only .svg-fill, .absolute-fill, .img-cover and the .text-* colours are used on a root page (index.html). The clamp, truncate, aspect, tabular and empty-collapse classes are shared but unused; pages still write -webkit-line-clamp and font-variant-numeric inline.
Preview 
<!-- Dynamic image: the box holds layout, the image crops -->
<div class="aspect-4-3">
  <img class="img-cover" src="/path/to/image.jpg" alt="" loading="lazy">
</div>

<h3 class="line-clamp-2">Backend title that may run long</h3>
<span class="truncate">Single-line label</span>
<span class="tabular-nums">1,240</span>
<p class="collapse-when-empty"></p>

<!-- Decorative shape behind an icon, coloured on the element -->
<span style="position:relative">
  <svg class="absolute-fill text-sage" viewBox="0 0 200 200" aria-hidden="true">...</svg>
</span>

Use it when

  • Wrap every dynamic image in an .aspect-* box and give the <img> .img-cover, so backend images of any size keep the grid aligned
  • .line-clamp-N on backend titles and excerpts, .truncate on single-line labels such as city names
  • .tabular-nums on prices, stats and counts so digits line up
  • .collapse-when-empty on optional backend fields, .flex-shrink-safe on flex children holding long text
  • .text-* and .bg-* to apply a theme colour on the element itself

Avoid

  • Re-authoring the same declaration inline or in a page block. Add the class
  • A per-variant colour selector (.X-card--tips .X-icon). Put .text-terracotta on the icon
  • A page <style> base rule on the same property: page styles load after styles.css and beat the utility
  • A one-property spacing class named after a section. Name slots by role, and reuse the existing ones
  • An <img> sizing itself inside a grid

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.svg-fillclassdisplay:block, 100% width and height. An inline svg fills its box.
.absolute-fillclassposition:absolute, inset 0, full size. The parent needs position:relative.
.img-coverclassBlock image, full size, object-fit:cover. Paints a warm placeholder when src is empty or broken.
.aspect-1-1 / -3-2 / -4-3 / -4-5 / -3-4 / -16-9 / -16-10 / -21-9classaspect-ratio plus overflow hidden and position relative.
.line-clamp-1 / -2 / -3 / -4classClamps text to N lines.
.truncateclassOne line with an ellipsis.
.tabular-numsclassTabular digits.
.collapse-when-emptyclassdisplay:none when the element is :empty.
.flex-shrink-safeclassmin-width:0 on a flex child.
.text-terracotta / -turmeric / -indigo / -sage / -sand / -aubergine / -espresso / -ink / -mutedclassSets color to the token.
.bg-terracotta / -turmeric / -indigo / -sage / -sand / -aubergineclassSets background-color to the token.

Source _dev/reference/components/utilities.html

Cards

Card hover lift

Paste In shared CSS

The standard hover for a bordered whole-card link: a 3px rise, a soft layered shadow and a slightly darker border. One co-class on the card root.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 1 page

index.html

Guidelines
styles.css holds only the :hover rule, so the host card must supply the border, radius and transition (the homepage .gt4-card does this in an inline style block). The class lifts the <a> itself, which conflicts with the memory rule that hover transforms belong on an inner, non-interactive element.
Preview 
<a href="#" class="my-card card-hover-lift">
  <!-- card content; the card rule sets its own border, radius and
       transition: transform .25s ease, box-shadow .25s ease, border-color .25s ease -->
</a>

Use it when

  • A bordered card whose whole surface is one link (GharTalks episodes, GharEvents cards on the homepage)
  • Cards that pair with a .btn-link cue inside, which reacts to the same card hover

Avoid

  • A per-section .x-card:hover copy of the same lift, shadow and border values
  • transition-all. Give the card a targeted transition on transform, box-shadow and border-color
  • Cards with no border and no surface, such as image-led editorial cards. They zoom the media instead
  • Relying on it where edge clicks must be reliable. The portal rule is that the element receiving the click never moves on hover; this class moves the card root

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.card-hover-liftclassCo-class on the card root. Paints only the :hover state: translateY(-3px), a two-layer shadow and border-color rgba(26,23,20,.14).
transitiontokenNot included. The card's own rule sets transition: transform .25s ease, box-shadow .25s ease, border-color .25s ease.

Source _dev/reference/components/card-hover-lift.html

Editorial image card

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

The design-pillar story card in three shapes: a 4:5 overlay card with the title over a soft scrim and a dek that opens on hover, an editorial card with a 4:3 image above the text, and a 16:9 lead card that can carry a sponsored strip.

NeedsNothing beyond the page
Where
Used on 3 pages

design-architecture.html design-series.html design.html

Guidelines
Canonical copy is the inline block in design-architecture.html (identical in voices.html and several other pages that do not render the markup). design.html carries a drifted copy with extra --wide, --quartet and __media--initials rules and a different --lead. On --ed cards, .hr-card__eyebrow--paid paints the eyebrow in brand red, against the portal rule that eyebrows are never red.
Preview 
<!-- Overlay card (4:5) -->
<a href="#" class="hr-card">
  <div class="hr-card__media"><img src="https://placehold.co/600x750" alt="Image description" loading="lazy" decoding="async"></div>
  <div class="hr-card__overlay" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  <div class="hr-card__body">
    <span class="hr-card__eyebrow">Category</span>
    <h3 class="hr-card__title">Story title</h3>
    <p class="hr-card__sub">Byline &middot; City</p>
    <div class="hr-card__dek-wrap"><p class="hr-card__dek">One sentence that tells the reader what the story is about.</p></div>
  </div>
</a>

<!-- Editorial card: image above text -->
<a href="#" class="hr-card hr-card--ed">
  <div class="hr-card__thumb">
    <div class="hr-card__media" style="background-image:url('https://placehold.co/900x675')"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="hr-card__body">
    <span class="hr-card__eyebrow">Category &middot; 8 min read</span>
    <h3 class="hr-card__title">Story headline that can run to two or three lines</h3>
    <p class="hr-card__sub">By Author name</p>
  </div>
</a>

<!-- Lead card (16:9) with sponsored strip -->
<a href="#" class="hr-card hr-card--lead">
  <div class="hr-card__media" style="background-image:url('https://placehold.co/1600x900')"></div>
  <div class="hr-card__overlay" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  <div class="hr-card__sponsored-strip">
    <span class="hr-card__sponsored-label">Featured project</span>
    <span class="hr-card__sponsored-by">Sponsored by <strong>Brand name</strong></span>
  </div>
  <div class="hr-card__body">
    <span class="hr-card__eyebrow hr-card__eyebrow--paid">Category</span>
    <h2 class="hr-card__title">Lead story headline</h2>
    <p class="hr-card__sub">By Brand name</p>
    <div class="hr-card__dek-wrap"><p class="hr-card__dek">Two sentences that set up the story. They open under the title on hover.</p></div>
  </div>
</a>
.hr-card{position:relative;display:block;overflow:hidden;border-radius:var(--r,16px);text-decoration:none;color:inherit;transition:transform .35s ease,box-shadow .35s ease;isolation:isolate;aspect-ratio:4/5;width:100%;will-change:transform;-webkit-mask-image:-webkit-radial-gradient(white,black)}
.hr-card:hover{transform:none;box-shadow:0 24px 48px -24px rgba(26,23,20,.22)}
.hr-card__media{position:absolute;inset:0;background-size:cover;background-position:center;border-radius:inherit;transition:transform .7s ease;overflow:hidden}
.hr-card__media img{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;display:block}
.hr-card:hover .hr-card__media{transform:scale(1.05)}
.hr-card__overlay{position:absolute;inset:0;background:linear-gradient(to top,rgba(26,23,20,.72) 0%,rgba(26,23,20,.42) 32%,rgba(26,23,20,.12) 58%,rgba(26,23,20,0) 78%);z-index:1}
.hr-card__body{position:absolute;bottom:0;left:0;right:0;padding:22px;z-index:2;color:#fff}
.hr-card__eyebrow{font:600 10px/1 'Inter',sans-serif;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:rgba(255,255,255,.82);margin:0 0 10px;display:inline-block}
.hr-card__eyebrow--paid{color:#e8c598}
.hr-card__title{font-family:var(--ff-display, 'Gazpacho', Georgia, serif);font-size:clamp(15px,1.25vw,19px);line-height:1.22;letter-spacing:-.005em;margin:0;color:#fff;font-weight:700;display:-webkit-box;-webkit-box-orient:vertical;-webkit-line-clamp:3;overflow:hidden}
.hr-card:not(.hr-card--ed) .hr-card__title{text-shadow:0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.35)}
.hr-card__sub{font:500 12px/1.4 'Inter',sans-serif;color:rgba(255,255,255,.72);margin:6px 0 0}
.hr-card__dek-wrap{display:grid;grid-template-rows:0fr;transition:grid-template-rows .4s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),margin-top .4s ease;margin-top:0}
.hr-card__dek{font:400 12px/1.55 'Inter',sans-serif;color:rgba(255,255,255,.82);margin:0;overflow:hidden;opacity:0;transition:opacity .3s ease .05s}
.hr-card:hover .hr-card__dek-wrap{grid-template-rows:1fr;margin-top:10px}
.hr-card:hover .hr-card__dek{opacity:1}
.hr-card--lead{aspect-ratio:16/9}
.hr-card--lead .hr-card__title{font-size:clamp(24px,2.6vw,40px);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.01em}
.hr-card--lead .hr-card__body{padding:clamp(24px,3vw,36px)}
.hr-card--lead .hr-card__dek{font:400 14px/1.6 'Inter',sans-serif;color:rgba(255,255,255,.88);max-width:640px;margin:0}
.hr-card--lead:hover .hr-card__dek-wrap{margin-top:14px}
.hr-card__sponsored-strip{position:absolute;top:0;left:0;right:0;z-index:3;padding:18px 24px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;background:linear-gradient(to bottom,rgba(0,0,0,.55) 0%,rgba(0,0,0,0) 100%);pointer-events:none}
.hr-card__sponsored-label{font:600 10px/1 'Inter',sans-serif;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#e8c598;flex-shrink:0}
.hr-card__sponsored-by{margin-left:auto;font:500 11px/1 'Inter',sans-serif;color:rgba(255,255,255,.82)}
.hr-card__sponsored-by strong{color:#fff;font-weight:600}
@media(max-width:743.98px){
  .hr-card__sponsored-strip{padding:14px 16px;gap:10px}
  .hr-card__sponsored-label{font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.12em}
  .hr-card__sponsored-by{font-size:10px}
}
.hr-card--ed{aspect-ratio:unset;display:block;background:transparent;border-radius:0;overflow:visible;box-shadow:none !important;-webkit-mask-image:none}
.hr-card--ed:hover{transform:none;box-shadow:none}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__thumb{display:block;position:relative;aspect-ratio:4/3;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;margin-bottom:14px;isolation:isolate}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__media{position:absolute;inset:0;border-radius:inherit}
.hr-card--ed:hover .hr-card__media{transform:scale(1.04)}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__overlay{display:none}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__body{position:static;padding:0;color:var(--ink)}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__eyebrow{order:-1;color:var(--muted);margin:0 0 10px;font:700 10px/1 'Inter',sans-serif;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;display:block}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__eyebrow--paid{color:var(--accent,#ee324b);font-weight:700}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__title{font-family:'Gazpacho',Georgia,serif;font-weight:700;font-size:19px;line-height:1.22;color:var(--ink);margin:0;letter-spacing:normal;text-shadow:none}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__sub{color:var(--muted);margin:6px 0 0;font-size:12px;line-height:1.4}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__dek-wrap{display:block;margin-top:12px}
.hr-card--ed .hr-card__dek{font:400 13px/1.55 'Inter',sans-serif;color:var(--muted);opacity:1;margin:0;display:-webkit-box;-webkit-line-clamp:3;-webkit-box-orient:vertical;overflow:hidden}
.hr-card--ed:hover .hr-card__dek-wrap{margin-top:12px}

Use it when

  • Stories, projects and designers on the Architecture and Design pages
  • --ed for three-up rows of stories where the reader scans headlines under images
  • --lead for the single featured story or sponsored project that opens a block

Avoid

  • Pages outside the design family. The CSS is inline per page and not in styles.css
  • A card with no real image. Every shape is image-led
  • Scaling or lifting the whole link on hover. Only the media zooms; the overlay card gains a shadow
  • Stacking a sponsored strip on a card that already sits in a sponsored block

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.hr-cardclass4:5 overlay card. The whole card is the <a>.
.hr-card--edmodifierImage on top in .hr-card__thumb (4:3, 12px radius), text below in ink.
.hr-card--leadmodifier16:9 overlay card with a display-size title and a wider dek.
.hr-card__mediaslotBackground-image div or a wrapped <img>. Zooms on hover.
.hr-card__overlayslotBottom scrim for the overlay shapes. Hidden on --ed.
.hr-card__eyebrowslotCategory and read time. Add --paid for a sponsored or featured tile.
.hr-card__title / __subslotGazpacho title clamped to three lines, then byline or place.
.hr-card__dek-wrap > .hr-card__dekslotOne-line summary. Opens on hover on overlay cards, always shown and clamped to three lines on --ed.
.hr-card__sponsored-stripslotTop strip with .hr-card__sponsored-label and .hr-card__sponsored-by. Overlay shapes only.

Source _dev/reference/components/card-hr.html

Where

Guidelines
On phones a section may hide the list with its own rule, since the card acts as a gateway and the full list is on the linked page (design-system note). The catalog example adds .svg-fill to the icon SVG; the homepage markup does not.

Use it when

  • Three to six capability rows inside a product card (the SuperPro and Developer Mandate cards)
  • Any feature-row pattern, co-classed with a section class for placement

Avoid

  • A per-section prefix that repaints the same rows. Co-class the <ul> instead
  • Long descriptions. Each row is one line; the full detail lives on the destination page
  • Coloured or red icons. Icons inherit the text colour at 70% opacity

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.feat-listclassThe <ul>: 22px top padding under a hairline rule, 16px gap between rows. Collapses when empty.
.feat-list__itemclassOne row: a 22px icon column and the text column, 14px apart.
.feat-list__iconslotaria-hidden span holding a 24-unit stroke SVG; painted in --espresso at .7 opacity.
.feat-list__text > .feat-list__title + .feat-list__descslot13px semibold title over a 12.5px description.

Video play overlay

Paste In shared CSS

A 56px frosted dark play circle centred over a video thumbnail. The wrapper covers the thumbnail and ignores the pointer, so the whole card stays the link.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
Where
Used on 4 pages

design-article.html design-series.html design.html index.html

Guidelines
The hover state (darker fill, scale 1.08) is wired only to .gt4-card:hover and .ad4-card:hover in styles.css, so a new card type gets no hover response until it is added to that selector. The design-system entry describes a white glass pill with an ink icon; production paints a dark circle with a white icon.
Preview 
<div class="my-card-thumb">
  <img src="https://placehold.co/1280x720" width="1280" height="720" alt="Video title" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
  <div class="thumb-play"><div class="thumb-play-btn"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 5v14l11-7z"/></svg></div></div>
</div>

Use it when

  • Any card whose thumbnail stands for a video: GharTalks episodes, Architecture and Design home tours, VideoWorks reels
  • Thumbnails inside a whole-card link that opens or plays the video

Avoid

  • A per-section play button or a new glass circle. Reach for .thumb-play
  • Making the circle its own button or link. The wrapper is pointer-events: none so the card receives the click
  • Photos that are not video. The play mark promises playback

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.thumb-playclassAbsolute inset-0 flex wrapper, z-index 2, pointer-events none. The thumbnail must be position: relative.
.thumb-play-btnclass56px circle, rgba(0,0,0,.45) with a 6px backdrop blur; holds an 18px white play glyph.
.rail-outer.is-native .thumb-play-btnmodifierOn touch rails the blur is dropped for a flat rgba(0,0,0,.6) fill.

.ep-brands{display:block}
.ep-brands--ticker{position:relative; overflow-x:clip; overflow-y:visible; margin:48px calc(-1 * var(--pad-h,clamp(24px,4vw,56px))) 0; padding:0; cursor:grab; touch-action:pan-y; -webkit-mask-image:linear-gradient(to right,transparent 0,#000 6%,#000 94%,transparent 100%); mask-image:linear-gradient(to right,transparent 0,#000 6%,#000 94%,transparent 100%)}
.ep-brands--ticker.is-dragging{cursor:grabbing; user-select:none}
.ep-brands--ticker.is-dragging a{pointer-events:none}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-ticker-track{display:flex; width:max-content; gap:0; align-items:stretch; padding:0 clamp(24px,4vw,56px); will-change:transform}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand{flex:0 0 auto; width:clamp(260px,21vw,340px); padding:32px 36px; text-decoration:none; color:inherit; display:flex; position:relative}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand::before{content:""; position:absolute; left:0; top:50%; transform:translateY(-50%); width:1px; height:64%; background:rgba(17,17,17,.07); pointer-events:none}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand:first-child::before{display:none}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__card{background:transparent !important; border:0 !important; border-radius:0; box-shadow:none !important; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; justify-content:flex-start; gap:14px; width:100%; transition:transform .25s ease}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand:hover .ep-brand__card{transform:translateY(-2px)}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__logo{height:80px; width:100%; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__wordmark{font-family:'Gazpacho',Georgia,serif; font-weight:700; font-size:clamp(16px,1.3vw,20px); letter-spacing:.04em; text-align:center; line-height:1.1; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink,#111)}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__info{text-align:center; width:100%; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; gap:4px}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__name{font:600 11.5px/1.2 'Inter',sans-serif; letter-spacing:.16em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink,#111); margin:0}
.ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__desc{font:400 13px/1.5 'Inter',sans-serif; color:var(--muted,#6e655b); margin:8px 0 0; display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:2; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; overflow:hidden; max-width:260px; text-align:center}
@media(max-width:599px){
  .ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand{width:clamp(220px,70vw,280px); padding:26px 28px}
  .ep-brands--ticker .ep-brand__logo{height:64px}
}
/* After gsap and /ghar-ticker.js (both defer). */
(function init() {
  if (typeof initTicker !== 'function') { setTimeout(init, 50); return; }
  document.querySelectorAll('.ep-brands--ticker').forEach(function (outer) {
    var track = outer.querySelector('.ep-ticker-track');
    if (!track) return;
    initTicker({ outer: outer, track: track, itemSelector: '.ep-brand' });
  });
})();

Use it when

  • A long list of brands below a featured tier, where browsing the names matters more than stepping through them
  • Logo walls that would otherwise wrap into a tall grid

Avoid

  • A track with one copy of the items. The wrap relies on Set 1 plus an aria-hidden Set 2, or the row visibly jumps
  • Wordmarks or logos that change on hover. Only the card lifts 2px
  • Content the reader must act on in order. Use a paged card carousel with arrows
  • Writing a new marquee. Every ticker links /ghar-ticker.js and calls initTicker

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.ep-brands.ep-brands--tickerclassClip, drag surface and edge mask. Bleeds out by one --pad-h.
.ep-ticker-trackclassThe row GSAP translates. Holds Set 1 then Set 2.
.ep-brandclassOne brand link. Set 2 copies carry aria-hidden="true" and tabindex="-1".
.ep-brand__wordmarkslotGazpacho uppercase name when there is no logo file. Put an <img> in .ep-brand__logo instead when there is one.
.ep-brand__name / .ep-brand__descslotSmall caps name and a description clamped to two lines.
.is-draggingmodifierWritten on the outer while dragging; links stop taking pointer events.
initTicker(opts)JSouter, track, itemSelector; optional speed (0.5 px per frame), cooldownMs (1500), momentumMul (220), glideDur (0.45).

/* Touch detection, once, near the top of <body>. initCarousel also checks
   (pointer: coarse); this flag covers the S Pen case. */
(function () {
  var hasTouch = ('ontouchstart' in window) || ((navigator.maxTouchPoints || 0) > 0);
  var isTouch = hasTouch && window.innerWidth < 1024;
  window.__GHAR_IS_TOUCH__ = isTouch;
  if (isTouch) document.documentElement.classList.add('touch-device');
})();

Use it when

  • A horizontal row of small icon plus label chips that link out: cities, collections, topics
  • Browse-by rows where the reader scans many short options and picks one

Avoid

  • Writing your own drag, overflow or arrow code. The rail-outer, rail and initCarousel trio is the only carousel on the portal
  • Filtering a list on the same page. Category pills between a section head and its rail use the tag strip
  • Large cards. Substantial cards belong in the paged card carousel with a paginator below
  • Adding overflow-x: clip to the section around it. This rail bleeds past the section padding, and a clip on top of the bleed slices the chips at the max-width line

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.dc-sectionclassSection frame: max-width plus side padding. The rail inside bleeds back out by one --pad-h.
.dc-blockclassOne eyebrow plus rail group. Two blocks in a row get the standard vertical gap.
.rail-outer.dc-track-outerclassThe clip and drag surface. Negative --pad-h margins give the bleed.
.rail.dc-track.dc-cities-trackclassThe track GSAP translates. Keep role="list".
.dc-cityclassOne chip: 40px icon tile plus a nowrap label. Whole chip is the link.
.dc-fade--l / .dc-fade--rslotEdge fades. Pass both to initCarousel so they follow the scroll position.
.dc-arrow--prev / .dc-arrow--nextslotMid-line arrows, shown on hover from 1080px only and hidden at either end.
.is-overflowing / .is-start / .is-end / .is-nativemodifierState classes initCarousel writes on the outer. Style against them, never set them by hand.
initCarousel(opts)JSWires the rail. See the carousel-init entry for every option.

Use it when

  • Wiring any .rail-outer / .rail pair: chips, cards, pills, portraits, modal chip rows
  • Picking the stepping model per rail with snap: 'card' for chips, 'page' for paged cards, 'free' for pill strips

Avoid

  • Inlining a second copy of the function on a page. Link /ghar-carousel.js once, after GSAP
  • Writing per-section drag, overflow or arrow code, or a new .x-track-outer fork
  • Setting .is-overflowing, .is-start, .is-end, .is-native, .is-peeking or .is-centered by hand. The function owns them
  • Keying native scroll on a surface or width. The device decides, through (pointer: coarse) and the touch flag

API

NameTypeWhat it does
initCarousel(opts)JSWires one rail. Call once per rail after GSAP and /ghar-carousel.js have loaded; it waits for gsap itself if needed.
outerattributeRequired. The .rail-outer clip and drag surface; state classes land here.
trackattributeRequired. The .rail child that is translated.
prevBtn / nextBtnattributeOptional paginator buttons outside the rail. Get disabled and .is-disabled at the ends.
arrowPrev / arrowNextattributeOptional in-rail hover arrows.
fadeL / fadeRattributeOptional edge fade elements that follow the scroll position.
snapattribute'card' (default) steps one card; 'page' steps floor(--n) cards; 'free' scrolls 70% of the viewport and glides.
widthModeattribute'auto' (default) keeps CSS widths; 'fractional-n' sizes cards from --n so floor(n) fit plus a peek, and toggles .is-peeking.
cssVarHost / nVarattributeElement to read the --n variable from, and its name (default '--n'). Pass cssVarHost explicitly.
autoplayMsattributeInterval in ms, 0 by default. Ticks only while the rail is in view, pauses on interaction and hover, off under reduced motion and for snap 'free'.
arrowExcludeSelectorattributeElements a pointerdown should not start a drag from. Default 'button'.
clickSlopPxattributePointer travel before a press becomes a drag and its click is swallowed. Default 5; modal chip rails pass 12.
centerMode / centerModeQueryattributeCentre the active card always, or only while a media query matches. Toggles .is-centered.
nativeScrollattributeForce browser scrolling. Otherwise chosen by (pointer: coarse) or window.__GHAR_IS_TOUCH__, which adds .is-native and an end spacer.
window.__GHAR_IS_TOUCH__attributeSet by the inline touch-detect snippet near the top of <body>, before any rail is wired.

Source _dev/reference/components/carousel-init.html

Use it when

  • Large portrait, project or editorial cards that need paged navigation
  • Any card row where the reader should see a peek of the next card at narrow widths

Avoid

  • Setting card widths in CSS. widthMode 'fractional-n' sets them from --n; your CSS only sets the --n curve on the block
  • Putting the paginator inside the head row. It auto-hides only as a sibling after the rail-outer
  • Showing arrows on a row that fits. The chassis hides the paginator when the rail is not overflowing; do not force it back
  • Small chips. Those use the chip carousel with in-rail arrows

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.dc-block--projectsmodifierCarries the --n and --gap curve: 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, then 3 cards from 1080px. Add your own co-class to set a different curve.
--n / --gaptokenCards visible and gap. A fractional --n makes the outer bleed and the next card peek (.is-peeking).
.rail-outer.dc-track-outerclassContained by default (overflow-x clip, no bleed), bleeds only while peeking or centred.
.dc-projclassProject card: full-bleed 4:5 image, fact pill, title, meta and price over a soft scrim. Whole card is the link.
.dc-paginatorclassCentred row of .dc-page-btn arrows below the rail. Hidden when the sibling rail is not overflowing.
.dc-paginator--sectionmodifierSection-rhythm spacing for a paginator that closes a whole section rather than a block.
.dc-page-btnclass44px round arrow. initCarousel sets disabled and .is-disabled at either end.
.is-peeking / .is-centeredmodifierWritten by initCarousel on the outer for fractional --n and for the centre-mode query.
initCarousel(opts)JSWires the rail with snap 'page', widthMode 'fractional-n' and centerModeQuery. See carousel-init.

Source _dev/reference/components/carousel-cards-paged.html

document.querySelectorAll('.tag-strip-outer').forEach(function (outer) {
  initCarousel({
    outer: outer,
    track: outer.querySelector('.tag-strip'),
    prevBtn: outer.querySelector('.tag-strip-arrow--prev'),
    nextBtn: outer.querySelector('.tag-strip-arrow--next'),
    snap: 'free'
  });
});

Use it when

  • Category or topic pills that link into a vertical, under a section head (Intelligence, Architecture and Design, GharEvents)
  • A pill row whose length depends on data and may or may not fit

Avoid

  • A new .x-pills-outer or .y-chips-wrap class just to set the gap under the strip. Co-class .section-pills-strip
  • Showing fades or arrows when the pills fit. They key off .is-overflowing, which initCarousel writes
  • Filter chips on a collection page. Collection pages carry no chip strip
  • Red pill text or red borders at rest. Only the icon turns brand red, on hover

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.rail-outer.tag-strip-outerclassClip and drag surface. Contained while it fits, bleeds by --pad-h once .is-overflowing.
.section-pills-stripclassStandard gap below the strip, clamp(28px, 3vw, 40px).
.section-pills-strip--gap-topmodifierAdds top breathing room when the strip does not follow a head directly.
.rail.tag-stripclassThe translated track. A <nav> with an aria-label naming the set.
.tag-strip-itemclassOne pill link: optional .tag-strip-item-icon (26px line icon) then the label.
.tag-strip-fade--l / --rslotEdge fades, visible only while overflowing and not at that end.
.tag-strip-arrow--prev / --nextslotHover arrows from 1080px, only while overflowing.
initCarousel(opts)JSOne loop over every .tag-strip-outer with snap 'free'. See carousel-init.

Use it when

  • The Spotlight placement on /brands and /people, above the directory grid
  • Rotating several paid or nominated tenants through one slot, one per day

Avoid

  • Painting the panel in the tenant's hex. Identity comes from their logo, their photography and one accent keyline; the surface stays white
  • A stock photo when a brand has no photography. The block is identity-led and the media is optional
  • Tenant-coloured CTAs. The CTA is ink-filled so its label passes contrast for any tenant
  • @media breakpoints inside the block. .if-block is a container; every breakpoint is @container
  • A Sponsored badge or section-level sponsorship wording without a disclosure decision

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.sp-sectionclassSection frame with max-width and padding. Add hidden to park it; the rotator inside is then skipped.
.sp-rotatorclassHolds one or more .sp-block children. Without JS the first shows; once wired only .is-active shows.
data-dedupe-grid / data-dedupe-cardattributeOn the rotator: the directory grid and card selectors. The card whose inner link matches the active block's href gets .is-spotlight-dupe.
.if-block.sp-block[data-kind]classOne tenant. data-kind is brand or person. container-type: inline-size.
.if-block__innerclassThe whole-block link. Carries --brand-canvas, --brand-text and, for people, --brand-soft.
.if-brandslot__lead photo (narrow only), __head with .if-logo, __name, __lead-copy, __meta spans and .if-cta, __chips (narrow), __work with three __tile images (from 760px).
.if-logo--darkmodifierDark tile for white-on-transparent logos. Never the brand's own hex.
.if-personslot__initial watermark, __portrait img, __body with __name and __role, __quote, __presence list, .if-cta. Third column from 880px.
.if-person__portrait--mono > .if-person__monomodifierMonogram in --brand-soft when there is no real portrait.
.is-active / .is-wired / .is-spotlight-dupemodifierWritten by gharSpotlightRotate. Never set by hand.
gharSpotlightRotate(rotator)JSPicks block days % count by local midnight, marks it active, hides its duplicate in the grid and calls grid.__revealReset() if present. main.js runs it on every .sp-rotator on load.

Checkbox, radio and switch

Paste In shared CSS

The small choice controls of the form system. The native input stays in the DOM and is visually replaced, so keyboard, submission and assistive tech work with no extra code. The whole label is the hit area.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
WhereNot on a shipped page yetGuidelines
Preview 
<!-- Checkbox: commits on submit -->
<label class="jm-check">
  <input type="checkbox" name="readyToMove">
  <span class="jm-check__box"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M20 6L9 17l-5-5"/></svg></span>
  <span>Ready to move in</span>
</label>

<!-- Radio: exactly one -->
<label class="jm-radio">
  <input type="radio" name="purpose" value="buy" checked>
  <span class="jm-radio__dot"></span>
  <span>I want to buy</span>
</label>
<label class="jm-radio">
  <input type="radio" name="purpose" value="rent">
  <span class="jm-radio__dot"></span>
  <span>I want to rent</span>
</label>

<!-- Switch: takes effect on flip -->
<label class="jm-switch">
  <input type="checkbox" name="priceAlerts" checked>
  <span class="jm-switch__track"></span>
  <span class="jm-switch__text">Price drop alerts<small>We message you when a saved home changes price.</small></span>
</label>

Use it when

  • Checkbox: a short list of words where several can be on, committed on submit
  • Radio: one answer out of a few (up to five)
  • Switch: a setting that takes effect the moment it flips, like a notification preference

Avoid

  • A switch inside a form that commits on submit. That is a checkbox
  • Radios past five options. Use a select
  • A set the reader should scan and compare (amenities, property type). Use chips or tiles
  • Removing the native input or hiding it with display:none, which breaks keyboard and form submission

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-checkclassCheckbox row on a <label>. Holds the native input, .jm-check__box and the text.
.jm-check__boxslotThe painted box. Carries the tick path M20 6L9 17l-5-5.
.jm-radioclassRadio row. Same shape as the checkbox, with .jm-radio__dot as the painted mark.
.jm-switchclassSwitch row, min-height 44px. Native checkbox plus .jm-switch__track and .jm-switch__text.
.jm-switch__text smallslotOptional second line under the switch label explaining what flipping it does.
disabledattributeOn the input. The row mutes and the cursor changes; the option stays visible.

Use it when

  • A question with two or three known, short, mutually exclusive answers
  • A step in a flow where the answer is recorded, not a view that swaps a panel

Avoid

  • Switching views or panels. That is the tab version of .seg with role=tablist
  • More than five answers (use a select) or answers that need explaining (use tiles)
  • .seg--ink beside a filled button. One filled object per view: pair the light thumb with a .btn-text step action
  • Wiring the setter to an inline onclick. Listen for the bubbling change event, or the arrow keys stop updating state

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.seg.seg--choiceclassThe group. Carries role=radiogroup and an aria-label.
.seg__btnclassEach answer: a button with role=radio. aria-checked is the only state; unchosen ones take tabindex=-1.
.seg__icoslotOptional two or three stroke line icon before the label, on currentColor.
.seg--inkmodifierDark thumb. Only on a surface with nothing else filled.
changeeventNative change fired on the chosen button and bubbling, from pointer and keyboard alike.
gharSegThumb(group, animate)JSRe-fits the thumb after you set aria-checked from code, or after a hidden group becomes visible. Pass false to land without the slide.
gharSegFit(group)JSRe-decides row versus stacked layout for a group whose container width changed without a resize.

Preview 
<select name="budget" class="jm-field" aria-label="Indicative budget">
  <option value="" selected>Indicative budget</option>
  <option value="under-25l">Under &#8377;25 lakh</option>
  <option value="25l-1cr">&#8377;25 lakh to &#8377;1 crore</option>

Use it when

  • Any list under about a dozen options inside a portal form
  • A select added after load (a modal body injected later): call initJmSelects on its container

Avoid

  • Hand-writing .jm-select markup. It is generated; write the plain select and let the script wrap it
  • A per-page custom dropdown (the old .brs-sort). This does it once for the form system
  • A list nobody can scan, such as countries or every city. That needs a searchable panel
  • Reading value from the visible trigger. Read the native select, which fires change as usual

API

NameTypeWhat it does
select.jm-fieldclassThe markup you write. First option is the prompt: value="" and, for required fields, disabled.
aria-labelattributeRequired. Copied to the generated trigger so it is announced.
initJmSelects(root)JSEnhances every select.jm-field inside root (default document). Runs on load; safe to call again, already enhanced selects are skipped.
data-jm-selectattributeSet by the script on each enhanced select as its idempotency guard. Never author it.
.jm-selectclassGenerated wrapper holding .jm-select__native (hidden), .jm-select__trigger and .jm-select__panel of .jm-select__opt rows. Flips up with .jm-select--up near the viewport bottom.
changeeventFired on the native select when an option is picked, so existing listeners keep working.

Field label, required mark and help

Paste In shared CSS

A persistent label above a .jm-field, an optional red asterisk for a field that blocks submit, and a muted help line tied to the control. For long multi-section flows where a placeholder would vanish as the reader types.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css
WhereNot on a shipped page yetGuidelines
Preview 
<label class="jm-label" for="carpetArea">Carpet area<span class="jm-req" aria-hidden="true">*</span></label>
<input type="text" class="jm-field" id="carpetArea" name="carpetArea" placeholder="e.g. 1,240" inputmode="numeric" required aria-describedby="carpetAreaHelp">
<small class="jm-help" id="carpetAreaHelp">The usable floor area inside your walls, in square feet. Not built-up or super built-up.</small>

<label class="jm-label" for="reraNumber">RERA registration number</label>
<input type="text" class="jm-field" id="reraNumber" name="rera" placeholder="e.g. P51800000000">
<small class="jm-help">Optional for resale. Required for any under-construction listing.</small>

Use it when

  • Long flows such as Post Property or the SuperPro application, where the reader loses the thread halfway down
  • A field whose expected answer needs one line of explanation (carpet area versus built-up)

Avoid

  • Short modals (sign in, contact, brief). They stay placeholder-driven; do not add labels just because you can
  • Colouring the label red. Only the asterisk carries the functional red
  • Help text that repeats the label in other words. If it adds nothing, delete it
  • Help text without aria-describedby, which strands it for screen readers

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-labelclassLabel above the control, 13px 600 ink. Always a real <label for>.
.jm-reqclassRed asterisk inside the label. aria-hidden, since the input carries required.
.jm-helpclassMuted help line under the control. Negative top margin tucks it against the field.
aria-describedbyattributeOn the control, pointing at the help line's id so it is announced with the field.

Source _dev/reference/components/form-label.html

Guidelines
Debt: gharBriefSubmit in main.js does not use gharFieldError yet. It paints its own .is-invalid class (styled only under #brBriefModal) and writes every message into .brf-error. New forms use gharFieldError.
Preview 
<!-- Per-field error: the message is bound to the control -->
<input type="tel" class="jm-field" id="ownerPhone" name="phone" placeholder="Mobile number" inputmode="numeric" aria-describedby="ownerPhoneErr">
<p class="jm-field-err" id="ownerPhoneErr" role="alert" hidden>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><path d="M12 8v5M12 16h.01"/></svg>
  <span></span>
</p>

<!-- Valid and disabled -->
<input type="tel" class="jm-field is-valid" value="+91 98765 43210" readonly aria-label="Verified mobile number">
<input type="text" class="jm-field" value="Mumbai" disabled aria-label="City, locked to Mumbai">

<!-- Form-level error, above the submit button -->
<p class="brf-error" id="formError" role="alert" hidden>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><path d="M12 8v5M12 16h.01"/></svg>
  <span id="formErrorText"></span>
</p>
var phone = document.getElementById('ownerPhone');

// Set: red border, message shown, aria-invalid="true"
gharFieldError(phone, 'Enter a 10 digit mobile number.');

// Clear: all three reset together
gharFieldError(phone, null);

Use it when

  • Telling the reader one field is wrong: a named cause and the shape of a valid answer, shown after they leave the field
  • A form-level summary above the submit button when the form as a whole cannot be sent (.brf-error)
  • A confirmed value that genuinely helps, such as a verified phone number (.is-valid)

Avoid

  • Toggling .is-error or the message by hand. Always go through gharFieldError so border, text and aria-invalid move together
  • Swapping the two: .jm-field-err is per field, .brf-error is the form-level summary
  • Apologetic or vague copy. Say what happened and how to fix it
  • Green on every correct field. Most correct fields need no colour; sage is only for a confirmation that helps
  • A toast for one field's error

API

NameTypeWhat it does
gharFieldError(field, message)JSSets the error on a control: adds .is-error, sets aria-invalid, writes the message into the element its aria-describedby names and unhides it. Pass null to clear.
.is-errormodifierRed border on .jm-field. Set by gharFieldError, not by hand.
.is-validmodifierSage border on .jm-field, for a confirmation that helps.
.jm-field-errclassPer-field message line with its icon. Starts hidden; its id goes in the control's aria-describedby.
.brf-errorclassForm-level error strip above submit, role=alert, hidden until needed.
disabledattributeWarm grey fill and muted text. Disabled, never hidden.

Use it when

  • Every text, email, phone, select or textarea control on the portal, in a modal or on a page
  • Short forms, which stay placeholder-driven: each control says what it is inside itself
  • Two short related answers side by side (type and city, budget and timeline) with .brf-row

Avoid

  • A separate select or textarea class. .jm-field covers all of them, and adding one is how a fork starts
  • A third prefix (.form-*, .brf-input). Extend .jm-* instead
  • Brand tints on a control. Form UI stays warm and monochrome, even on a tenant page
  • Placeholder-only controls on a long multi-section form: those need a persistent label

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-fieldclassThe control. Put it on input, select and textarea alike: 1.5px rule border, 14px radius, ink border on focus.
.jm-phoneclassMobile number wrapper. The inner input takes no class; the wrapper draws the box.
.jm-phone-prefixslotStatic flag and +91 before the input. The sign-in modal swaps this for the searchable country-code button.
.brf-rowclassTwo controls on one line as a 1fr 1fr grid. Drops to one column below 560px. The only layout class a form needs.
aria-labelattributeRequired on every select, whose first disabled option doubles as its visible label.

Use it when

  • A form that genuinely has sections, such as Post Property or the SuperPro application
  • A textarea with a maxlength the reader should see coming (data-counter)
  • A secondary plus primary action pair at the end of a form or dialog

Avoid

  • Fieldsets in a six-field modal. Short forms need none of this
  • Putting the primary on the left. Secondary sits left, the most committed action keeps the rightmost position
  • A red legend. The legend is an eyebrow: 10px, uppercase, faint
  • .jm-btn--danger anywhere but an irreversible action in a confirm dialog

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-fieldsetclassA <fieldset> group. Adjacent fieldsets get a hairline and top padding between them.
.jm-legendclassThe group's <legend>, styled as an eyebrow. A following <p> becomes its muted intro.
data-counterattributeOn a textarea or input: the id of its .jm-counter. Paints used / maxlength on input and on load. Self-wiring.
.jm-counterclassRight-aligned tabular count under the control. Gets .is-over at the limit.
.jm-actionsclassOne row of buttons, 12px apart.
.jm-btnclassThe form button: full width on its own, shared across flex space in .jm-actions.
.jm-btn--primarymodifierThe commit. One per view.
.jm-btn--secondarymodifierWhite with a field rule; the non-committing action.
.jm-btn--dangermodifierRed fill, only for the irreversible action in a confirm dialog.

    </span>

Use it when

  • A set the reader scans and compares: amenities, configuration, the whole filter sheet (chips)
  • Two to a handful of options that each need a sentence, such as construction stage or furnishing (tiles)
  • Options carrying a third-party logo, via the white logo plate

Avoid

  • A solid ink selected fill. The 2px ink outline carries the state; a black logo on an ink fill disappears
  • Brand rose, blush, petal or mist, or an ink alpha, as a selected fill. Foundation tones only
  • Hiding an unavailable option. Disable it so the reader knows it exists
  • A count of zero shown as a live chip. Disable it
  • Setting an .is-selected class from JS. State follows the input through :has()
  • Two or three fixed, mutually exclusive answers. That is the either/or control

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-chip-rowclassWrapping flex row of chips. Wraps rather than scrolls so nothing hides off-screen.
.jm-chipclassA pill on a <label> holding a checkbox (many on) or radio (exactly one). Clears 48px.
.jm-chip--smmodifierDense chip for filter sheets. Still clears 40px.
.jm-chip__iconslotOptional line icon on currentColor.
.jm-chip__countslotMuted result count after the label.
.jm-chip__logoslotWhite plate holding a partner mark so the selection fill never lands behind it.
.jm-chip__logo--darkmodifierDark plate for white-on-transparent marks. Same on .jm-tile__logo--dark.
.jm-tile-gridclassauto-fit grid with a 260px floor, so two columns become one on a phone without a breakpoint.
.jm-tileclassA block option with .jm-tile__icon (or __logo) and .jm-tile__body holding __title and __desc.
.jm-tile--stackmodifierIcon above text, for picture-led tiles. Pair with .jm-tile__check.
.jm-tile__checkslotOpt-in tick badge, only where a border alone reads as decoration.

      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Use it when

  • Deleting or withdrawing something that cannot come back: a listing, an account, a sent application

Avoid

  • Anything reversible. Do it immediately and offer Undo in a toast instead
  • OK or Yes on the destructive button. It carries the action's own verb (Delete listing)
  • Describing the mechanism. Name the consequence the reader has to weigh
  • The destructive button on the left, or a red fill anywhere else in the form system

Use it when

  • A set of images a visitor wants to see full size, such as certificates: wrap each thumbnail in a link to the large image with data-fancybox="group" and data-caption
  • Binding a group once with Fancybox.bind and passing options through gtFancybox.mergeDefaults

Avoid

  • PDFs. Leave data-fancybox off so the link opens the file in a new tab
  • Adding Toolbar or Panzoom overrides to fix mobile. Earlier custom configs killed Fancybox's built-in drag, pinch and double-tap
  • Styling .fancybox__container or .fancybox__backdrop without checking gt-fancybox.js, whose interceptors key off those nodes
  • A light lightbox. Image viewing is one of the few surfaces reserved for a dark overlay

API

NameTypeWhat it does

data-captionattributeCaption text shown with the image.

gtFancybox.mergeDefaults(options)JSPass-through for shared options; installs the portal tap interceptors (idempotent; the file also installs them itself on DOMContentLoaded) and returns the options unchanged today.
