Preview 
<div id="exampleOverlay" class="jm-overlay"></div>
<div id="exampleModal" class="jm-modal jm-size-lg" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="exampleModalTitle">
  <div class="jm-hdr">
    <div class="jm-heading" id="exampleModalTitle">Share your project brief</div>
    <button class="jm-close" type="button" aria-label="Close">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M18 6L6 18"/><path d="M6 6l12 12"/></svg>
    </button>
  </div>
  <div class="jm-body">
    <p class="jm-subtext">Tell us what you are building.</p>
    <form>
      <input type="text" name="name" class="jm-field" placeholder="Your name" required autocomplete="name">
      <button type="submit" class="jm-btn jm-btn--primary">Send</button>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>
var overlay = document.getElementById('exampleOverlay');
var modal = document.getElementById('exampleModal');
var lastTrigger = null;

function openExample(trigger) {
  lastTrigger = trigger || null;
  overlay.classList.add('jm-open');
  modal.classList.add('jm-open');   // main.min.js adds body.jm-scroll-locked + history
}
function closeExample() {
  overlay.classList.remove('jm-open');
  modal.classList.remove('jm-open');
  if (lastTrigger) lastTrigger.focus();  // focus returns to the trigger
}
overlay.addEventListener('click', closeExample);
modal.querySelector('.jm-close').addEventListener('click', closeExample);
document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
  if (e.key === 'Escape' && modal.classList.contains('jm-open')) closeExample();
});

Use it when

  • A task that genuinely cannot continue underneath: signing in, sending a brief, contacting a brand, confirming something irreversible
  • Any new modal. Start from these classes instead of an ID block of its own

Avoid

  • Sticky or fixed chrome inside the modal. The body scrolls everything together, header and close included
  • position:fixed on body to lock scroll, or visualViewport height syncing. The lock is the body.jm-scroll-locked class, nothing else
  • Leaving role="dialog" off. main.min.js finds modals by it to add the scroll lock and back-button close
  • A dark modal by default on a dark page. Modals stay light unless the content is inherently dark (.jm-modal--dark)
  • var(--ink) as a primary button fill on a dark tenant, where --ink is remapped to cream. Use the red primary
  • Opening without a way back: overlay click, the close button and Escape must all close it

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.jm-overlayclassFixed backdrop, z-index 310, 50% black with a 2px blur and touch-action:none so iOS cannot rubber-band the page behind.
.jm-modalclassFixed centred panel, z-index 315, 20px radius, max-height min(92vh, 820px). Needs role="dialog", aria-modal and a label.
.jm-size-sm | -md | -lg | -xlmodifier420, 480, 540, 660px (capped at 92vw). sm a confirm, md sign in or a short form, lg a standard form, xl only for real horizontal need.
.jm-openmodifierOn both overlay and modal: fades and scales in. Removing it closes.
.jm-hdrclassTitle row: title left, close right, hairline below. Not sticky.
.jm-hdr-titleslotInter 14px 600 utility title for functional modals (Sign In, a confirm).
.jm-headingclassGazpacho editorial title for content modals. A child <span> gives the two-line preamble plus subject (Contact / Brand).
.jm-subtextclassMuted dek under the heading.
.jm-closeclass36px round close. Inside .jm-hdr, or as the first child of .jm-modal for a title-less modal (floats right, flex-end).
.jm-bodyclassOwns the padding and is the only scroll container, with overscroll-behavior:contain. A form inside becomes a 14px gap column.
.jm-modal--no-fullscreenmodifierKeeps a tiny confirm as a centred card on phones instead of the full-screen sheet.
.jm-modal--dark / .jm-overlay--darkmodifierOpt-in dark surface (#0F0F0F, cream title) and a heavier 70% backdrop, for inherently dark content.
body.jm-scroll-lockedbody classAdded by main.min.js (and dist/bpr-reveal.js on brand profiles) while any [role=dialog] carries .jm-open. overflow:hidden !important; never set it yourself.
historyeventOpening pushes a history entry and the device Back button closes the modal, via the same hook. Register a close function in knownCloseFor for modals with teardown.

Source _dev/reference/components/modal-shell.html

A short confirmation or error that appears at the edge of the screen. One function creates the host, stacks them, times them out and animates them away.

Use it when

  • Confirming something the reader just did: saved, copied, sent
  • An error that is not tied to one form field
  • Offering a single Undo right after an action

Avoid

  • Writing .toast markup by hand. The host, stacking and timers only exist in gharToast
  • An error about one field: use the field error state instead
  • Anything the reader must read to continue. Errors already persist; a decision needs a dialog

API

NameTypeWhat it does
gharToast(title, opts)JSShows a toast. Returns dismiss(), so the caller can close it early.
opts.typeattributesuccess (default), info, warn or error. Errors are announced assertively.
opts.bodyattributeA second line, for detail the title cannot carry.
opts.durationattributeMilliseconds before it clears. 0 keeps it. Errors default to 0, everything else to 4000.
opts.actionattribute{ label, onClick } for one inline action such as Undo.

/* syncH(): publish both measured heights (inline on every consumer). */
function syncH(){
  var mh = mainNav.getBoundingClientRect().height;
  document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--mainnav-h', mh + 'px');
  if (subnav){
    var sh = subnav.getBoundingClientRect().height;
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--subnav-h', sh + 'px');
  }
}

/* In the page's scroll-collapse handler: hide L1 only through the gate. */
document.body.classList.toggle('mainnav-hidden', shouldCollapse && !!(window.gharCanCollapseNav && window.gharCanCollapseNav()));

Use it when

  • A vertical hub and its sibling pages where the section tabs are the primary navigation (design, voices, ghartalks)
  • Any page that wants the masthead to hide on scroll: L1 may only collapse when this bar is there to take the top

Avoid

  • A third bar. A second axis (series, franchise) is an in-page block or the .dp-subnav strip on the page where that axis is the operative one
  • A tab strip on a results page whose finder already scopes the set (voices-search hides it below 1080)
  • Toggling body.mainnav-hidden without the gharCanCollapseNav() gate. On desktop the tabs live inside L1 and would leave with it
  • Hand-setting --subnav-h. syncH() publishes it from the measured height, and 0 is the signal that the bar is merged
  • Per-page tweaks to a shared vertical's bar (extra active states, hash shims). Sibling pages keep it byte-identical
  • Using it on /brands, /people or person profiles, whose handoff target is the sticky finder, not an L2 bar

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.subnavclassThe bar. Sits inside #navStack right after the nav partial.
.subnav-innerclassThe tab row. This is the node the merge moves into #navTabs at 1080px and up, so scope tab styling to it, not to .subnav.
.subnav-linkclassOne tab: .subnav-icon over a label span.
.activemodifierOn the current tab, together with aria-current="page". Ink underline, weight 600.
.subnav-ruleclassThe chevron hairline before the tabs. Hidden on content-nav pages, where the masthead lockup already names the section.
gharCanCollapseNav()JSTrue only when --subnav-h is greater than 0, i.e. a separate L2 bar exists to take the top of the viewport.
--subnav-htokenMeasured bar height, published by syncH(). Body top padding is --mainnav-h + --subnav-h.
body.subnav-mergedbody classSet when the tabs have moved into the masthead (1080px and up, content-nav pages).
body.mainnav-hiddenbody classTranslates #navStack up by --mainnav-h, leaving this bar at the top.

<!-- Measure mainNav height so body padding-top accounts for fixed positioning. -->
<script>
(function(){
  var mainNav = document.querySelector('#mainNav');
  if (!mainNav) return;
  function syncH(){
    var mh = mainNav.getBoundingClientRect().height;
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--mainnav-h', mh + 'px');
  }
  syncH();
  window.addEventListener('resize', syncH, { passive: true });
  if (document.readyState !== 'complete'){
    window.addEventListener('load', syncH, { once: true });
  }
})();
</script>

Use it when

  • Every portal page that is not a microsite (brand and person profiles run their own topbar)
  • body.simple-nav: an inner page with one centred search pill instead of the homepage's expanded bar
  • body.simple-nav content-nav: editorial and directory pages. Adds the G + section lockup and removes Post Property, the search pill and the mobile bottom bar
  • body.cta-subscribe on editorial streams (design, voices, ghartalks); body.cta-brief on directories (brands, people); neither on a page with nothing to ask for
  • body.nav-search only together with the page's own handler for .nav-btn--search

Avoid

  • Pasting or editing the markup. Everything between the PARTIAL markers is regenerated, and the build reports success while discarding a hand edit
  • A per-page nav. Add the control to partials/nav.html and switch it on with a body class
  • Adding the page to PAGES in build-partials.mjs without adding it to VERTICAL_LOCKUP (or BARE_BY_DESIGN). The lockup label is stripped silently and the page ships a bare G
  • body.nav-search without a handler: it ships a dead button
  • Hiding the masthead on scroll on a page with no second-level bar. Gate it with gharCanCollapseNav()
  • Forcing a white nav background. #mainNav matches the page canvas through --warm-white

Guidelines
No page on the partial system uses this full bar today: every partial consumer is simple-nav or content-nav. The only live copy is index.html, which carries its own inline nav markup and nav CSS rather than the partial, so the two can drift.

Use it when

  • The homepage and commerce pages, where property search is the page's job
  • Any new search entry point: reuse .search-trigger and call openMobileSearch() instead of authoring a second bar

Avoid

  • Editorial and directory pages. body.content-nav removes it on purpose: a property search pill competes with the reading, and /brands and /people have their own finders
  • Relabelling it 'Search Design' or pointing it at content. It searches listings; a vertical finder is its own modal
  • Re-authoring the bar, its chips or its suggestion panel in a page. The logic is all in main.js
  • A search with no city. Focusing Where with no city forces the city gate open first

API

NameTypeWhat it does
#searchBarslotThe expanded pill (Where, Mode, Type, Go). Shown at 1080px and up on pages without simple-nav.
#compactSearchslotThe collapsed pill past scrollY 8. Clicking it force-opens the full bar with a .nav-overlay dimmer.
.search-triggerclassSurface class shared by #compactSearch, #midSearchTrigger (992 to 1079), #midSmallTrigger (744 to 991, and every simple-nav page) and #mobSearchTrigger (below 744).
.chip-scrollclass#chipsRow, the horizontal locality chip strip. .is-scrolled adds the left fade mask. Two chips inline, the rest collapse to +N.
#cityChipHostslotThe pinned city chip, outside the scrolling strip so it never clips.
#wherePanelslotSuggestion panel under Where: popular items idle, grouped matches while typing.
openMobileSearch()JSEvery collapsed trigger opens the search modal. The expand and collapse of the bar itself is private to main.js (collapseNav / expandNav inside a closure) and is not callable.

Use it when

Avoid

NameTypeWhat it does

Scroll reveal

Call In shared CSS

Fades content in once as it scrolls into view. The page lists selectors and a primitive per selector; the script adds the classes, an IntersectionObserver adds .is-revealed once, and CSS runs the transition.

Needs/dist/reveal.min.css/dist/bpr-reveal.js
Where
Used on 23 pages

brand-profile-asian-paints.html brand-profile-avirahi.html brand-profile-godrej-properties.html brand-profile-horizon-architects.html brand-profile-obeetee.html brand-profile-saint-gobain.html brand-profile-scarlet-splendour.html brand-profile-studiofov.html brand-profile-teearch.html person-profile-adi-godrej.html person-profile-ashish-bajoria.html person-profile-darshini-mahadevia.html person-profile-devesh-motta.html person-profile-hardik-shah.html person-profile-hemal-shah.html person-profile-hiten-motta.html person-profile-manpreet-singh.html person-profile-pirojsha-godrej.html person-profile-satish-bhansali.html person-profile-suman-kanodia.html person-profile-tarun-motta.html person-profile-vinod-doshi.html person-profile-virendra-shah.html

Guidelines
dist/bpr-reveal.js also carries two unrelated portal blocks for pages that do not load main.min.js: the image graceful-load (js-imgfx) and the modal back-button plus body scroll lock hook, both mirrored in main.js by hand. Its header comment still says the reveal CSS lives in brand-profile.min.css; it moved to dist/reveal.min.css. Only brand and person profiles use it.
Preview 
/* Right before </body>, after <script src="/dist/bpr-reveal.js"></script> */
if (typeof bprReveal === 'function') bprReveal({
  map: [
    [".pp-about",             "js-cascade--rise"],
    [".bpr-intel-grid",       "js-cascade--print"],
    [".pp-contact",           "js-reveal--rise"]
  ]
});

Use it when

  • Brand and person profile sections: reading content rises, cards print in, split heroes slide from each side
  • js-cascade on a grid or list, so its direct children stagger in
  • js-reveal--fade on a rail whose children already carry carousel transforms

Avoid

  • Writing js-reveal classes into markup by hand. Authoring stays clean; bprReveal adds them from the map
  • Replaying on scroll-back. Each element reveals once and is unobserved
  • Adding the classes server-side. The hidden state must only exist once the script runs, so content stays visible if JS or IntersectionObserver is missing
  • Animating anything but transform and opacity, or ignoring prefers-reduced-motion (the CSS already snaps to the end state)
  • A second copy of the observer inline in a tenant. Every tenant calls the one in /dist/bpr-reveal.js

API

NameTypeWhat it does
bprReveal({ map, threshold, rootMargin })JSmap is a list of [selector, class] rows. threshold defaults to 0.15, rootMargin to "0px 0px -60px 0px". Selector misses are silent.
js-reveal--risemodifierSlow fade and 28px rise. Reading content. Also --print (quick scale), --split-l, --split-r (slide from a side), --bloom (scale from .85 with overshoot), --fade (opacity only).
js-cascade--risemodifierTargets the element's direct children with nth-child delays from .05s to .5s. Also --print and --bloom.
.is-revealedmodifierAdded once when the element intersects.

Source _dev/reference/components/scroll-reveal.html

NameTypeWhat it does

a.hv-cue[data-hv-scroll]attributeHero pill. Smooth-scrolls to its href (default #film) below the .bpr-topbar, then plays. Hidden on mobile.

Photo lightbox

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

Opens an article photo full-size with a caption, and steps through every photo in the same figure. Self-hosted PhotoSwipe; each image is a plain link to the high-res file, so it still works with JS off.

Needs/dist/photoswipe/photoswipe.css
Where
Used on 2 pages

design-article.html voices-article.html

The trigger CSS, the caption CSS and the module init are copied inline, identically, in design-article.html, voices-article.html and ghartalks-article.html. PhotoSwipe 5.4.4 is vendored in dist/photoswipe; no page loads the dynamic-caption plugin files vendored beside it.
Preview 
<figure data-pswp-gallery>
  <a class="pswp-link"
     href="https://placehold.co/2400x1600"
     data-pswp-width="2400"
     data-pswp-height="1600"
     data-pswp-caption="Caption for the photo. <em>Photography &middot; Credit</em>"
     aria-label="Open photo at full size">
    <img src="https://placehold.co/2000x1333" alt="Describe the photo" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
  </a>
  <figcaption>Caption for the photo.</figcaption>
</figure>
/* In the page <style> */
.pswp-link {
  display: block;
  position: relative;
  cursor: zoom-in;
  -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
}
.pswp-link::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  top: 12px;
  right: 12px;
  width: 36px;
  height: 36px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background:
    url("data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 24 24' fill='none' stroke='%23111' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round'><path d='M15 3h6v6M14 10l7-7M9 21H3v-6M10 14l-7 7'/></svg>")
    center / 16px no-repeat,
    rgba(255, 255, 255, .92);
  opacity: 0;
  transform: translateY(-3px);
  transition: opacity .2s ease, transform .2s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1);
  pointer-events: none;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, .12);
}
.pswp-link:hover::after,
.pswp-link:focus-visible::after {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: translateY(0);
}
/* Don't double up zoom-in indicator on small carousel cards */
@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .pswp-link::after { display: none; }
}

/* Caption strip at the foot of the open lightbox */
.pswp__caption {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
  padding: 16px 24px 22px;
  max-width: 720px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  font: 400 13px/1.55 'Inter', sans-serif;
  color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .85);
  text-align: center;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.pswp__caption em { font-style: italic; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .65); }
<script type="module">
  import PhotoSwipeLightbox from '/dist/photoswipe/photoswipe-lightbox.esm.min.js';
  const lightbox = new PhotoSwipeLightbox({
    gallery:    '[data-pswp-gallery]',
    children:   'a.pswp-link',
    pswpModule: () => import('/dist/photoswipe/photoswipe.esm.min.js'),
    // `fade` open/close is more forgiving than `zoom` when the thumb
    // crops the image to a different aspect ratio than the hi-res.
    showHideAnimationType: 'fade',
    bgOpacity: 0.95,
    paddingFn: () => ({ top: 30, bottom: 60, left: 0, right: 0 }),
  });
  lightbox.on('uiRegister', function() {
    lightbox.pswp.ui.registerElement({
      name: 'caption',
      order: 9,
      isButton: false,
      appendTo: 'root',
      html: '',
      onInit: (el, pswp) => {
        pswp.on('change', () => {
          const slide = pswp.currSlide;
          const cap = slide?.data?.element?.dataset?.pswpCaption || '';
          el.innerHTML = cap;
        });
      },
    });
  });
  lightbox.init();
</script>

Use it when

  • Inline images and photo carousels in long-form articles (design, voices and GharTalks articles)
  • Grouping: every a.pswp-link inside one [data-pswp-gallery] figure becomes one prev/next set

Avoid

  • Brand profile galleries, which use Fancybox
  • Omitting data-pswp-width and data-pswp-height. PhotoSwipe needs the real size of the high-res file to lay the slide out
  • An <a> without a real href to the large image. That link is the no-JS fallback
  • Loading the lightbox eagerly. The core module is imported only when a photo is opened

API

NameTypeWhat it does
[data-pswp-gallery]attributeOn the <figure>. One gallery group per element.
.pswp-linkclassThe anchor around each image. href is the high-res file; cursor zoom-in and an expand badge on hover (hidden under 600px).
data-pswp-width / data-pswp-heightattributePixel size of the high-res image.
data-pswp-captionattributeHTML caption shown at the foot of the open lightbox (the .pswp__caption element registered in the init).

Source _dev/reference/components/photo-lightbox.html

Use it when

  • The one playable video on an episode or article page (the GharTalks episode hero)
  • Chapter timestamps under that player: .gtk-chapter[data-t] seeks the page's [data-gtk-play] host
  • Listing cards that show a video still: put the same facade inside the card's <a> and it stays a link

Avoid

  • Embedding a YouTube iframe on load. A player costs about a megabyte and hundreds of ms of main thread per instance
  • Expecting a facade inside an <a href> to play. The handler deliberately declines there so the card navigates to the episode page
  • Self-hosting video. Films are YouTube embeds
  • Writing a page-local click handler. main.min.js handles every [data-gtk-play] and .art-video__frame[data-video-id], including ones rendered later
  • Brand profile films: those use the film block and /dist/hv-video.js

API

NameTypeWhat it does
[data-gtk-play]attributeThe YouTube video id. Carry role="button" tabindex="0" and an aria-label; Enter and Space play it.
[data-gtk-title]attributeTitle given to the iframe once it mounts. Defaults to 'GharTalks episode'.
[data-gtk-playing]attributeSet on the host after mounting, so a second click does nothing.
.gtk-facade__playclassThe play disc. .gtk-facade__dur is the duration chip.
.gtk-chapter[data-t]attributeSeconds to seek to. Mounts the player at that start, sets aria-current, and scrolls to the player only if it is off-screen.
.art-video__frame[data-video-id]attributeThe older article-catalog facade, handled by the same code. Its CSS is inline in the article pages.
[data-yt-fallback]attributeOn the still: the video id to fall back to hqdefault.jpg when maxresdefault is missing. Handled by an inline script on the GharTalks pages, not by main.min.js.

Brand profile contact card

Paste In shared CSS

The closing card on every brand profile: title, a short lead, the Contact button that opens the shared contact modal, optional reach rows, and info blocks for office and response time. Every colour is a --contact-* token, so a tenant themes it light or dark without touching a rule.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css/dist/brand-profile.min.css
Where
Used on 9 pages

brand-profile-asian-paints.html brand-profile-avirahi.html brand-profile-godrej-properties.html brand-profile-horizon-architects.html brand-profile-obeetee.html brand-profile-saint-gobain.html brand-profile-scarlet-splendour.html brand-profile-studiofov.html brand-profile-teearch.html

Guidelines
Painted twice: dist/brand-profile.min.css (body .bpr-contact__*) and dist/styles.min.css (body :is(.pp-contact__inner, .bpr-contact__inner)) both style the card at the same specificity, and brand-profile.min.css wins by load order. Three tokens tenants declare (--contact-spine-width, --contact-cta-padding, --contact-cta-fontsize) are consumed nowhere, and the five --contact-panel-* tokens only reach a .bpr-contact__cta panel the current brand markup no longer renders. asian-paints, obeetee and saint-gobain declare no tokens and sit at the 1.07:1 fallback; whether to change them is an open user decision (docs/PROFILE-TEMPLATIZATION-STATE.md).
Preview 
<!-- Tenant tokens live in the tenant's :root. Light tenant: set at least --contact-surface.

      <button type="button" class="bpr-btn bpr-btn--primary bpr-contact__cta-btn" data-brand-contact data-brand="Brand Name">
        Contact
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 5l7 7-7 7"/></svg>
      </button>
      <ul class="bpr-contact__reach">
        <li class="bpr-contact__reach-row">
          <span class="bpr-contact__reach-icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 6a2 2 0 012-2h12a2 2 0 012 2v12a2 2 0 01-2 2H6a2 2 0 01-2-2V6z"/><polyline points="4 7 12 13 20 7"/></svg></span>
          <div class="bpr-contact__reach-body">
            <span class="bpr-contact__reach-label">Email</span>
            <a class="bpr-contact__reach-value" href="mailto:hello@example.com">hello@example.com</a>
          </div>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </div>

    <div class="bpr-contact__info">
      <div class="bpr-contact__info-block">
        <span class="bpr-contact__info-icon" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M21 10c0 7-9 13-9 13s-9-6-9-13a9 9 0 0118 0z"/><circle cx="12" cy="10" r="3"/></svg></span>
        <span class="bpr-contact__info-label">Head office</span>
        <p class="bpr-contact__info-body">Office address as supplied by the brand</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

Use it when

  • The Contact section at the end of a brand profile, directly above the microfooter. It is required on every brand category
  • Theming a tenant's card: set the --contact-* tokens in that tenant's :root and nothing else
  • Rendering whatever contact data the brand provided: drop reach rows or info blocks that have no real data

Avoid

  • Building a new tenant by pasting this section. A tenant starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-{family}.html through the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile, which already carries the card
  • Setting background, color or border on .bpr-contact__inner in page CSS. dist/brand-profile.min.css uses body .bpr-contact__* selectors (0-1-1), so a page rule (0-1-0) silently loses, and a direct background bypasses --contact-surface and leaves light ink on a pale card
  • Leaving the tokens undeclared on a white page. --contact-surface falls back to #faf7f2, which measures 1.07:1 against white and the card disappears
  • A cross-brand formula for the tokens. Each tenant tunes its own block; a shared formula was tried twice and rejected
  • A brand-tinted card surface or a coloured edge stripe. The brand appears once, on the CTA
  • Using it on a person profile. People use .pp-contact, a deliberately different card
  • Inventing a response time, hours or an address. Info blocks carry only what the brand supplied

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.bpr-contactclassSection wrapper. id="contact" is load-bearing: the reach and info rows are styled through #contact selectors in dist/brand-profile.min.css (without it the icons render at full width), and the topbar and sticky bar link to it.
.bpr-contact__innerclassThe card. Paints --contact-surface, --contact-border, --contact-ink and the ::after glow.
.bpr-contact__introslotLeft column: title, lead, CTA and optional reach rows.
.bpr-contact__cta-btnclassCo-classed with .bpr-btn .bpr-btn--primary. Carries data-brand-contact data-brand="Brand Name" so the shared contact modal opens with the brand's name.
.bpr-contact__reachslotOptional list of .bpr-contact__reach-row (icon, label, value link). Only for channels the brand published.
.bpr-contact__infoslotRight column of .bpr-contact__info-block items (icon, label, body). Holds one to three blocks without looking half empty. Icons use currentColor, never var(--brand).
data-brand-contactattributeHook read by the shared contact modal script. data-brand sets the modal heading.
--contact-surfacetokenCard background. Fallback #faf7f2. Dark tenants set a near-black (#12181f). Teearch and Studio FOV set #ffffff because their page ground is warm-white.
--contact-inktokenCard text and title colour. Fallback var(--ink). Dark: #f5f2ec.
--contact-ink-mutedtokenLead and meta rows. Fallback var(--muted). Dark: rgba(245,242,236,.72).
--contact-eyebrow-colortokenThe small eyebrow painted by .bpr-contact__title::before (and .pp-contact__eye). Fallback var(--muted). Dark: rgba(245,242,236,.7).
--contact-bordertokenCard outer border. Fallback var(--rule). Dark: rgba(255,255,255,.06).
--contact-dividertokenHairlines inside the card. Only read by .pp-contact__meta-icon in styles.min.css; no brand-profile rule consumes it today. Dark tenants set rgba(255,255,255,.10).
--contact-panel-bgtokenInset CTA panel fill. Read only by .bpr-contact__inner > .bpr-contact__cta and .pp-contact__cta. The current brand markup has no __cta panel, so this is inert on brand profiles. Fallback transparent.
--contact-panel-bordertokenInset panel border colour. Same scope as --contact-panel-bg. Fallback transparent.
--contact-panel-border-widthtokenInset panel border width. Same scope. Fallback 0; dark tenants set 1px.
--contact-panel-radiustokenInset panel radius. Same scope. Fallback 0; dark tenants set 18px.
--contact-panel-paddingtokenInset panel padding. Same scope. Fallback 0; dark tenants set clamp(28px, 3vw, 36px).
--contact-spine-widthtokenDeclared by dark tenants (0, to disable the old spine hairline) but read by no rule in any shipped stylesheet. Setting it has no effect.
--contact-cta-bgtokenCTA button fill and the tint of its glow shadow. Fallback var(--brand, var(--ink)). Dark tenants use cream (#f5f2ec) or the brand hex.
--contact-cta-fgtokenCTA text and arrow. Fallback #ffffff. Pair a cream CTA with the surface colour (#12181f).
--contact-cta-hover-bgtokenCTA hover fill. Fallback: --contact-cta-bg mixed 88% with 12% black.
--contact-cta-paddingtokenDeclared by Godrej and Scarlet Splendour (18px 30px) but read by no rule in any shipped stylesheet. No effect.
--contact-cta-fontsizetokenDeclared by Godrej and Scarlet Splendour (15px) but read by no rule in any shipped stylesheet. No effect.
--contact-glow-alphatokenOpacity (0 to 1) of the radial glow in .bpr-contact__inner::after. Fallback 0 (no glow). Dark tenants use .35 to .38.

Source _dev/reference/components/brand-profile-contact.html

Brand profile hero, graphic (no media)

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

The opening of a brand profile for a brand with no primary visual: a light split hero with the copy column on the left, a quiet ambient line graphic on the right, and a full-width strip below holding the metrics card and the facts and socials row.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css/dist/brand-profile.min.css
Where
Used on 2 pages

brand-profile-studiofov.html brand-profile-teearch.html

Guidelines
Status is inline: this CSS lives in each page's own style block. The @style is the hero CSS from _dev/templates/brand-profile-service.html with the TEEARCH-only ambient drawing animations (.ah-* classes and te* keyframes) removed, plus the .bpr-hero__graphic img rules from brand-profile-studiofov.html. Production state: no page yet uses the decoupled img. The template and teearch inline a tenant-specific animated SVG (whose ambient > svg rules hide strokes until those .ah-* animations draw them), Studio FOV inlines its own SVG (.bpr-hero__graphic--sfv) while also carrying the unused img rules, and _default.svg is only mentioned in comments. Only teearch and studiofov use this hero. On phones the img has no sizing rule of its own (the mobile band rules target ambient > svg), so it renders at min(46vw, 640px) in the corner of the band instead of filling it; the pattern needs a mobile rule before any tenant adopts it. The .is-hero-loaded trigger script is inline per page. The template's main hero CSS is about 42 KB inline per page.

.bpr-hero { position: relative; min-height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden; background: #1a1714; color: #fff; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: flex-end; padding: 0 !important; }

(function () {
  var hero = document.querySelector('.bpr-hero--split');
  if (!hero) return;
  requestAnimationFrame(function () {
    requestAnimationFrame(function () {
      hero.classList.add('is-hero-loaded');
    });
  });
})();

Use it when

  • Service brands (architecture, consultancy, advisory, studios) that have no strong photograph of their own. This is the service family hero
  • The first section inside main.bpr-page, with --brand and --brand-soft set on main
  • The graphic is a decoupled asset: /brand_assets/brand-graphics/{slug}.svg, falling back to /brand_assets/brand-graphics/_default.svg, so the hero never ships another tenant's drawing
  • Metrics carry the track-record receipts (founded, count of projects, empanelments). Up to four, each a real figure from the brand's own material

Avoid

  • Image-led brands. If the brand has real project or product photography, use brand-profile-hero-photo
  • A stock or AI photograph dropped into the ambient slot to make it photo-led
  • Placeholder metrics on a live page. If there are no verified figures, drop .bpr-hero__metrics and keep the meta row
  • A brand colour wash behind the hero. The ground stays the page tone; the brand hex is for the logo tile, badge and CTA only
  • Painting the logo tile in the brand hex. White or dark tile only, even though the modifier is called --brand
  • Building a new tenant by pasting this section. A new brand starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-service.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.bpr-hero--splitclassSplit layout modifier on .bpr-hero: light ground, copy left, ambient graphic right. On phones the graphic moves above the copy as a 44vh band.
.is-hero-loadedclassAdded to .bpr-hero--split two animation frames after load by the page script in @js. On phones every copy element sits at opacity 0 until it lands, so the hero is blank without the script.
.bpr-hero__ambientclassAbsolutely placed, pointer-events none, aria-hidden container for the graphic.
.bpr-hero__graphicclassThe decoupled img. Sized to min(40vw, 560px) on desktop, opacity .72, with a slow reveal and float. Swaps to _default.svg on error.
.bpr-hero__labelsclassRow holding the tier badge and the eyebrow.
.bpr-hero__logo--brandclassLogo tile variant used by the split hero. Still a white or dark tile.
.bpr-hero__stripclassFull-width band under the copy that holds the metrics and the meta row.
.bpr-hero__metricsclassBordered metrics card; each .bpr-hero__metric has a Gazpacho .bpr-hero__metric-num and a small .bpr-hero__metric-label. Four across, two by two under 900px.
.bpr-hero__meta-rowclassFacts (.bpr-hero__facts) and hover-expand social pills (.bpr-hero__socials), same markup as the photo hero.
--brand / --brand-softtokenSet inline on main.bpr-page. Tint the badge and small accents only.

Source _dev/reference/components/brand-profile-hero-graphic.html

Brand profile hero, photo-led

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

The full-height opening of an image-led brand profile: a real brand photograph under a dark scrim, the logo tile, tier badge, eyebrow, brand name, one-line promise and a quiet meta row of facts and hover-expand social pills. On phones the photo sits above a light card that holds the copy, with the logo tile straddling the seam.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css/dist/brand-profile.min.css
Where
Used on 7 pages

brand-profile-asian-paints.html brand-profile-avirahi.html brand-profile-godrej-properties.html brand-profile-horizon-architects.html brand-profile-obeetee.html brand-profile-saint-gobain.html brand-profile-scarlet-splendour.html

Guidelines
Status is inline because almost all hero CSS lives in each page's own style block; dist/brand-profile.min.css only carries a few base rules and the keyframes. The @style here is the hero CSS from _dev/templates/brand-profile-developer.html (about 12 KB). Drift: the seven photo-hero tenants (asian-paints, avirahi, godrej-properties, horizon-architects, obeetee, saint-gobain, scarlet-splendour) carry six different copies of this CSS, and none matches the developer template byte for byte (only asian-paints and saint-gobain agree). The .bpr-hero__overlay block is dead on every profile (hidden by shared CSS) yet still shipped with about 1 KB of inline CSS.

.bpr-hero { position: relative; min-height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden; background: #1a1714; color: #fff; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: flex-end; padding: 0 !important; }
.bpr-hero__bg { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; }
.bpr-hero__bg img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; transform: scale(1.08); animation: bprKenBurns 22s ease-in-out infinite alternate; }
.bpr-hero__scrim { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(0,0,0,.42) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 22%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 45%, rgba(0,0,0,.78) 100%), linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,.34) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 55%); pointer-events: none; }
.bpr-hero__inner { position: relative; z-index: 2; max-width: var(--max-w); width: 100%; margin: 0 auto; padding: clamp(88px, 10vh, 112px) var(--pad-h) clamp(56px, 7vh, 88px); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: clamp(16px, 2vw, 24px); }
.bpr-hero__logo { padding: 12px 20px; min-height: 72px; min-width: 72px; max-width: 260px; width: fit-content; align-self: flex-start; border-radius: 16px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule); -webkit-backdrop-filter: none; backdrop-filter: none; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; margin: 0 0 clamp(4px, 1vw, 12px); box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(26,23,20,.08), 0 12px 32px -12px rgba(26,23,20,.2); }
.bpr-hero__logo img { max-height: 48px; max-width: 220px; width: auto; height: auto; object-fit: contain; display: block; }
.bpr-hero__logo__fallback { font-family: 'Gazpacho', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 22px; color: #fff; line-height: 1; }
.bpr-hero__logo.bpr-hero__logo--dark { background: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); -webkit-backdrop-filter: none; backdrop-filter: none; }
.bpr-hero__eyebrow { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; font: 600 11px/1 'Inter', sans-serif; letter-spacing: .18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(255,255,255,.82); }
.bpr-hero__name { font-family: 'Gazpacho', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 72px); line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -.022em; color: #fff; margin: 0; max-width: 16ch; text-wrap: balance; }
.bpr-hero__tagline { max-width: 540px; font: 400 clamp(16px, 1.35vw, 20px)/1.55 'Inter', sans-serif; color: rgba(255,255,255,.86); margin: 0; }
.bpr-hero__actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; margin: 8px 0 0; }
.bpr-hero__actions .bpr-btn--light { background: #fff; color: var(--ink); border-color: #fff; }
.bpr-hero__actions .bpr-btn--light:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,.9); gap: 14px; }
.bpr-hero__actions .bpr-btn--ghost { background: transparent; color: #fff; border-color: rgba(255,255,255,.4); }
.bpr-hero__actions .bpr-btn--ghost:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,.1); border-color: #fff; gap: 14px; }
.bpr-hero__meta-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 14px 32px; margin-top: 12px; padding-top: 24px; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.16); font: 500 13px/1.4 'Inter', sans-serif; color: rgba(255,255,255,.78); }
.bpr-hero__meta-row span { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
.bpr-hero__meta-row svg { width: 14px; height: 14px; opacity: .6; flex-shrink: 0; }
.bpr-hero__socials { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; flex-shrink: 0; }
.bpr-hero__social-wrap { display: inline-flex; flex: 0 0 auto; }
.bpr-hero__social { position: relative; width: 36px; min-width: 36px; height: 36px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 0; border-radius: 999px; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; overflow: visible; background: rgba(255,255,255,.10); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(140%); backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(140%); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.22); transition: background .25s ease, border-color .25s ease; }
.bpr-hero__social:hover, .bpr-hero__social:focus-visible { color: #fff; outline: none; -webkit-backdrop-filter: none; backdrop-filter: none; }
.bpr-hero__social--ig:hover, .bpr-hero__social--ig:focus-visible { background: #E4405F; border-color: #E4405F; }
.bpr-hero__social--yt:hover, .bpr-hero__social--yt:focus-visible { background: #FF0000; border-color: #FF0000; }
.bpr-hero__social--web:hover, .bpr-hero__social--web:focus-visible { background: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); }
.bpr-hero__social--li:hover, .bpr-hero__social--li:focus-visible { background: #0A66C2; border-color: #0A66C2; }
.bpr-hero__social-icon { width: 14px; height: 14px; flex-shrink: 0; display: block; }
.bpr-hero__social-label { position: absolute; bottom: calc(100% + 10px); left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); padding: 7px 11px; background: #1a1410; color: #fff; border-radius: 6px; font: 500 12px/1.3 'Inter', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0; white-space: nowrap; max-width: min(320px, 80vw); opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 5; transition: opacity .2s ease, transform .2s ease; order: initial; overflow: visible; margin: 0; }
.bpr-hero__social-label::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 100%; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); border: 5px solid transparent; border-top-color: #1a1410; }
.bpr-hero__social:hover .bpr-hero__social-label, .bpr-hero__social:focus-visible .bpr-hero__social-label { opacity: 1; transform: translateX(-50%) translateY(-2px); }
.bpr-hero__facts { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 14px 28px; }
.bpr-hero__meta-row:has(.bpr-hero__socials) { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 20px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .bpr-hero__meta-row { color: var(--muted); border-top-color: var(--rule); }
  .bpr-hero__facts { justify-content: center; color: var(--muted); }
  .bpr-hero__facts svg { opacity: .5; }
  .bpr-hero__meta-row:has(.bpr-hero__socials) { flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; gap: 18px; }
  .bpr-hero__socials { flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; width: 100%; gap: 8px; }
  .bpr-hero__social-wrap { width: 100%; display: block; }
  .bpr-hero__social { width: 100%; min-width: 0; height: 48px; padding: 0 16px; gap: 12px; justify-content: flex-start; background: rgba(26,23,20,.04); color: var(--ink); border-color: rgba(26,23,20,.14); -webkit-backdrop-filter: none; backdrop-filter: none; }
  .bpr-hero__social:hover, .bpr-hero__social:focus-visible { color: #fff; background: var(--brand, var(--ink)); border-color: var(--brand, var(--ink)); }
  .bpr-hero__social-label { order: 1; position: static; transform: none; background: transparent; color: inherit; padding: 0; border-radius: 0; display: inline-block; max-width: none; opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; margin: 0; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.2; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; flex: 1; min-width: 0; z-index: auto; }
  .bpr-hero__social-label::after { display: none; }
  .bpr-hero__social:active { transform: scale(.99); }
}
.bpr-hero__logo, .bpr-hero__eyebrow, .bpr-hero__name, .bpr-hero__tagline, .bpr-hero__actions, .bpr-hero__meta-row, .bpr-hero__metric { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px); animation: bprHeroIn .95s cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .2, 1) forwards; }
.bpr-hero__logo { animation-delay: .08s; }
.bpr-hero__eyebrow { animation-delay: .22s; }
.bpr-hero__name { animation-delay: .34s; }
.bpr-hero__tagline { animation-delay: .58s; }
.bpr-hero__actions { animation-delay: .74s; }
.bpr-hero__metric:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: .82s; }
.bpr-hero__metric:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: .89s; }
.bpr-hero__metric:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: .96s; }
.bpr-hero__metric:nth-child(4) { animation-delay: 1.03s; }
.bpr-hero__meta-row { animation-delay: 1.15s; }
.bpr-hero .bpr-badge { opacity: 0; transform: scale(.55); transform-origin: left center; animation: bprBadgePop .7s cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) forwards; animation-delay: .14s; }
.bpr-hero__metrics { opacity: 0; animation: bprHeroFade .7s cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .2, 1) .78s forwards; }
@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .bpr-hero .bpr-hero__logo { opacity: 0; transform: scale(.85); transform-origin: center center; animation: bprHeroLogoPop .7s cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) .35s forwards; }
  .bpr-hero .bpr-hero__name { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(22px); filter: blur(10px); animation: bprHeroNameIn 1.1s cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .2, 1) 1.25s forwards; }
  .bpr-hero .bpr-badge { animation-delay: .75s !important; animation-duration: .6s !important; }
  .bpr-hero .bpr-hero__eyebrow { animation-delay: 1.05s !important; }
  .bpr-hero .bpr-hero__tagline { animation-delay: 1.55s !important; }
  .bpr-hero .bpr-hero__meta-row { animation-delay: 1.85s !important; }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .bpr-hero__bg img { animation: none; transform: none; }
  .bpr-hero__logo, .bpr-hero__eyebrow, .bpr-hero__name, .bpr-hero__tagline, .bpr-hero__actions, .bpr-hero__meta-row, .bpr-hero__metrics, .bpr-hero__metric, .bpr-hero .bpr-badge { opacity: 1; transform: none; filter: none; animation: none; }
}
@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .bpr-hero__overlay { position: fixed; top: calc(env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) + 12px); left: 0; right: 0; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 0 16px; z-index: 46; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity .32s ease; }
  .bpr-hero__overlay > * { pointer-events: auto; }
  .bpr-hero__overlay-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 999px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.5); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(22px) saturate(1.8); backdrop-filter: blur(22px) saturate(1.8); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.22); box-shadow: 0 1px 6px rgba(26,23,20,.12), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.35); color: var(--ink); text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background .18s ease, transform .18s ease; }
  .bpr-hero__overlay-btn:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,.72); }
  .bpr-hero__overlay-btn:active { transform: scale(.96); }
  .bpr-hero__overlay-btn svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; display: block; }
  body[data-past-image] .bpr-hero__overlay { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }
}
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .bpr-hero__overlay { display: none; }
}
@media (max-width: 767px), (max-width: 1024px) and (orientation: portrait) {
  .bpr-hero { min-height: 0; display: block; background: #fff; overflow: visible; }
  .bpr-hero__bg { position: relative; inset: auto; height: 44vh; min-height: 320px; }
  .bpr-hero__scrim { height: 44vh; min-height: 320px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(0,0,0,0) 60%, rgba(0,0,0,.35) 100%); }
  .bpr-hero__inner { position: relative; margin-top: -24px; padding: 0 var(--pad-h) 32px; background: #fff; border-radius: 24px 24px 0 0; gap: 14px; z-index: 4; text-align: center; }
  .bpr-hero__logo { padding: 14px 20px; min-height: 76px; min-width: 76px; max-width: 240px; width: fit-content; border-radius: 16px; margin: -44px auto 8px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule); -webkit-backdrop-filter: none; backdrop-filter: none; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(26,23,20,.08), 0 12px 32px -12px rgba(26,23,20,.28); }
  .bpr-hero__logo img { max-height: 48px; max-width: 200px; width: auto; height: auto; object-fit: contain; image-rendering: -webkit-optimize-contrast; display: block; }
  .bpr-hero__logo__fallback { color: var(--ink); }
  .bpr-hero__logo--dark .bpr-hero__logo__fallback { color: #fff; }
  .bpr-hero__eyebrow { color: var(--muted); justify-content: center; align-self: center; }
  .bpr-hero__name { color: var(--ink); font-size: clamp(30px, 8vw, 44px); max-width: none; }
  .bpr-hero__tagline { color: var(--ink2); }
  .bpr-hero__actions { justify-content: center; }
  .bpr-hero__meta-row { gap: 10px 20px; padding-top: 18px; border-top-color: var(--rule); color: var(--muted); justify-content: center; }
  .bpr-hero__actions { display: none; }
}
@keyframes bprKenBurns { from { transform: scale(1.08) translate(0, 0); } to { transform: scale(1.16) translate(-2%, -1.5%); } }
@keyframes bprHeroIn { to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } }
@keyframes bprBadgePop { to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
@keyframes bprHeroFade { to { opacity: 1; } }
@keyframes bprHeroLogoPop { to { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } }
@keyframes bprHeroNameIn { to { opacity: 1; transform: none; filter: blur(0); } }

Use it when

  • Brands that own a strong primary visual (developers, material and product brands with real project or product photography). This is the developer family hero
  • The first section inside main.bpr-page, directly after the topbar
  • Facts carry orientation only (where they build, what they build). Founding year and track-record numbers belong in a metrics strip lower down

Avoid

  • Brands with no primary visual. Use brand-profile-hero-graphic (the service family split hero) instead of a stock or AI photo
  • A brand colour wash over the photo. The scrim is neutral; brand hex is reserved for the CTA, logo and small accents
  • Painting the logo tile in the brand hex. The tile is white (default) or .bpr-hero__logo--dark only
  • Omitting the onerror fallback on the logo img. It swaps in a monogram tile when the asset 404s
  • Building a new tenant by pasting this section. A new brand starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-developer.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile, which carries this hero and its CSS

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.bpr-heroclassSection. 100dvh, dark #1a1714 ground, content pinned to the bottom.
.bpr-hero__bgclassPhoto layer (aria-hidden) with a slow bprKenBurns drift; the img uses loading=eager. Its presence is what body:has(.bpr-hero__bg) keys on to give the topbar white ink.
.bpr-hero__scrimclassNeutral dark gradient that keeps the copy legible.
.bpr-hero__overlayclassMobile glass Back and Share discs (.bpr-hero__overlay-btn). Still in the template markup, but dist/styles.min.css sets body:is(.pp-page,[data-brand-format]) .bpr-hero__overlay{display:none!important}, so it never shows on a profile; the topbar and sticky bar carry these actions. Keep for parity, do not restyle it back without a decision.
.bpr-hero__logoclassWhite logo tile, flexes to the logo aspect. Add .bpr-hero__logo--dark for a dark tile. Holds .bpr-hero__logo__fallback when the image fails.
.bpr-badge--signature / .bpr-badge--featuredclassTier badge. Signature = Partner tier, Featured = Spotlight tier, omit for Presence tier.
.bpr-hero__eyebrow / .bpr-hero__name / .bpr-hero__taglineclassCategory line, the h1 and the one-line promise. Each rises in on load with a staggered delay.
.bpr-hero__meta-rowclassFacts (.bpr-hero__facts, icon + text spans) on the left, socials (.bpr-hero__socials) on the right.
.bpr-hero__social--web / --li / --ig / --ytclassRound social pill that expands to show .bpr-hero__social-label on hover or focus; each modifier sets its hover colour.

Source _dev/reference/components/brand-profile-hero-photo.html

Brand profile story (about)

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

The About chapter of a developer or product brand profile: a Story eyebrow, the brand's promise as a large pull quote, a strip of track-record metrics, then the story prose with a Continue reading collapse beside an In brief colophon of numbered receipts (segments, markets, recognition).

Needs/dist/styles.min.css/dist/brand-profile.min.css
Where
Used on 2 pages

brand-profile-avirahi.html brand-profile-godrej-properties.html

Guidelines
Status is inline: no bpr-story or bpr-receipt rule is in any shared stylesheet. Shipped on godrej-properties and avirahi (identical CSS, about 10 KB) and in a reduced form on asian-paints, horizon-architects, obeetee and saint-gobain, each with a different CSS copy; the developer template's copy differs again. The @style is Godrej's, and the read-more script in @js is Godrej's inline script, which also handles the service family's .bpr-about__body. The service family about (.bpr-about--seamless, 28 to 30 KB inline on teearch and studiofov with tenant drawings) was not catalogued as a separate component.
Preview 
<section class="bpr-sec bpr-sec--tight" id="about" data-previous-anchors="story">
<div class="bpr-story">
  <span class="bpr-story__eyebrow">Story</span>
  <figure class="bpr-story__quote">
    <span class="bpr-story__mark" aria-hidden="true">&ldquo;</span>
    <blockquote class="bpr-story__blockquote">The brand's own one-line promise, quoted.</blockquote>
    <figcaption class="bpr-story__cite">
      <span class="bpr-story__cite-line"></span>
      Brand Name &middot; since YYYY
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div class="bpr-story__metrics" aria-label="Portfolio at a glance">
    <div class="bpr-story__metric">
      <span class="bpr-story__metric-num">00<span class="bpr-story__metric-unit">+</span></span>
      <span class="bpr-story__metric-label">Metric label</span>
    </div>
    <div class="bpr-story__metric">
      <span class="bpr-story__metric-num">00<span class="bpr-story__metric-unit">+</span></span>
      <span class="bpr-story__metric-label">Metric label</span>
    </div>
    <div class="bpr-story__metric">
      <span class="bpr-story__metric-num">00<span class="bpr-story__metric-unit">+</span></span>
      <span class="bpr-story__metric-label">Metric label</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="bpr-story__grid">
    <div class="bpr-story__body">
      <p class="bpr-story__lead">Lead paragraph: what the brand is and who it builds for, in two sentences.</p>
      <p>Body paragraph from the brand's own site or client document: history, scale and what sets the practice apart. Key figures can be set in <strong>bold</strong>.</p>

    </div>
    <div class="bpr-story__readmore-row">
      <button type="button" class="bpr-story__readmore" data-readmore aria-expanded="false">
        <span data-readmore-label>Continue reading</span>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="14" height="14" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/></svg>
      </button>
    </div>
    <aside class="bpr-story__colophon" aria-label="What the brand stands for">
      <span class="bpr-story__colophon-label">In brief</span>
      <div class="bpr-receipt">

When .bpr-story__metrics enters the viewport, add .is-in-view (CSS animates opacity + translateY on the group) then roll each .bpr-story__metric-num from 0 up to its final value. Years (four digits, 1800-2100) count from target-25 for a tighter, less absurd reveal than 0000-1990. Respects reduced-motion. --> <script> (function () { if (!('IntersectionObserver' in window)) return; var reduced = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; function easeOutCubic (t) { return 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3); } function formatN (n) { return String(n).replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ','); } function rollNumber (textNode, target, isYear, raw) { var start = isYear ? Math.max(0, target - 25) : 0; var duration = isYear ? 1200 : 1500; var t0 = performance.now(); var final = raw; function tick (now) { var t = Math.min(1, (now - t0) / duration); var v = Math.round(start + (target - start) * easeOutCubic(t)); textNode.data = isYear ? String(v) : formatN(v); if (t < 1) requestAnimationFrame(tick); else textNode.data = final; } textNode.data = isYear ? String(start) : formatN(start); requestAnimationFrame(tick); } function animateStrip (strip) { strip.classList.add('is-in-view'); if (reduced) return; var nums = strip.querySelectorAll('.bpr-story__metric-num'); nums.forEach(function (el, i) { var textNode = el.firstChild; if (!textNode || textNode.nodeType !== 3) return; var raw = textNode.data.trim(); var target = parseInt(raw.replace(/,/g, ''), 10); if (isNaN(target)) return; var isYear = raw.length === 4 && target > 1800 && target < 2100; setTimeout(function () { rollNumber(textNode, target, isYear, raw); }, i * 120); }); } var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) { entries.forEach(function (entry) { if (!entry.isIntersecting) return; animateStrip(entry.target); io.unobserve(entry.target); }); }, { threshold: 0.35 }); document.querySelectorAll('.bpr-story__metrics').forEach(function (el) { io.observe(el); }); }
(function initAboutReadMoreOverflow () {
  var bodies = document.querySelectorAll('.bpr-about__body, .bpr-story__body');
  bodies.forEach(function (body) {
    var isStory = body.classList.contains('bpr-story__body');
    var basePrefix = isStory ? 'bpr-story' : 'bpr-about';
    var rowClass   = basePrefix + '__readmore-row';
    var innerClass = basePrefix + '__body-inner';
    var visibleMod = basePrefix + '__readmore-row--visible';
    var scope = body.parentElement;
    var row = scope && scope.querySelector('.' + rowClass);
    if (!row) return;
    var btn = row.querySelector('[data-readmore]');
    if (!btn) return;
    var inner = document.createElement('div');
    inner.className = innerClass;
    while (body.firstChild) inner.appendChild(body.firstChild);
    body.appendChild(inner);
    body.appendChild(row);
    function fadeColour () {
      var el = body;
      while (el && el !== document.documentElement) {
        var bg = getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor;
        if (bg && bg !== 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' && bg !== 'transparent') return bg;
        el = el.parentElement;
      }
      return getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor || '#ffffff';
    }
    body.style.setProperty('--readmore-fade', fadeColour());
    function pxVar (name, fallback) {
      var raw = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)
                  .getPropertyValue(name).trim();
      if (raw.endsWith('px')) return parseFloat(raw);
      if (raw.endsWith('vh')) return window.innerHeight * (parseFloat(raw) / 100);
      return fallback;
    }
    function shouldEnable () {
      return inner.scrollHeight > pxVar('--readmore-threshold', 1200) + 24;
    }
    var enabled = false;
    function apply () {
      if (shouldEnable()) {
        enabled = true;
        body.setAttribute('data-collapsed', 'true');
        row.classList.add(visibleMod);
      } else {
        enabled = false;
        body.removeAttribute('data-collapsed');
        row.classList.remove(visibleMod);
      }
    }
    var run = function () { apply(); };
    if (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready) {
      document.fonts.ready.then(run);
    } else {
      run();
    }
    var label = btn.querySelector('[data-readmore-label]');
    var chevron = btn.querySelector('svg');
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
      var collapsed = body.getAttribute('data-collapsed') === 'true';
      if (collapsed) {
        body.removeAttribute('data-collapsed');
      } else {
        body.setAttribute('data-collapsed', 'true');
      }
      btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', collapsed ? 'true' : 'false');
      if (label) label.textContent = collapsed ? 'Show less' : 'Continue reading';
      if (chevron) chevron.style.transform = collapsed ? 'rotate(180deg)' : '';
    });
    var resizeT;
    window.addEventListener('resize', function () {
      clearTimeout(resizeT);
      resizeT = setTimeout(function () {
        body.style.setProperty('--readmore-fade', fadeColour());
        var opened = body.getAttribute('data-collapsed') === null && enabled;
        if (opened) return; 
        apply();
      }, 150);
    });
  });
})();

Use it when

  • Developer family tenants, directly after the hero. id="about" is the topbar anchor; data-previous-anchors keeps old #story links working
  • Metrics are the credibility receipts that the photo hero deliberately leaves out: founding year, projects delivered, area, cities. Two to four, all verified
  • Long prose collapses on its own: the script shows Continue reading only when the body exceeds --readmore-threshold (1200px, 1600px on phones) and folds it to --readmore-fold-h. At normal copy length the button never renders, as on every live tenant

Avoid

  • Invented quotes, figures or awards. The quote is the brand's own line; every number comes from its site or client document
  • Service-family tenants. They use the seamless about card with a site-plan graphic (.bpr-about--seamless), not this layout
  • Em dashes in copy. Godrej's live prose still has two &mdash; entities
  • Building a new tenant by pasting this section. A brand starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-developer.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.bpr-sec--tightclassTighter section padding used for the story chapter.
.bpr-story__quoteclassPull quote figure: .bpr-story__mark glyph, .bpr-story__blockquote and a .bpr-story__cite with a hairline.
.bpr-story__metricsclassMetric strip; each .bpr-story__metric-num can hold a smaller .bpr-story__metric-unit.
.bpr-story__gridclassTwo columns on desktop: .bpr-story__body prose and the .bpr-story__colophon aside.
[data-readmore] / [data-readmore-label]attributeContinue reading toggle. The script wraps the body in .bpr-story__body-inner, measures overflow and adds .bpr-story__readmore-row--visible only when needed.
--readmore-threshold / --readmore-fold-h / --readmore-fadetokenCollapse trigger height (1200px, 1600px on phones), folded height (720px, 900px on phones) and fade colour, which the script repaints from the section background.
.bpr-receiptclassNumbered colophon row: .bpr-receipt__no, .bpr-receipt__label, .bpr-receipt__body.

Brand profile team rail

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

The Team section of a brand profile: a titled rail of person cards, each with a 4:3 portrait or a monogram tile in the tenant colour, name, role, city, expertise tags and a Connect button. Every card links to that person's /people profile.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css/dist/brand-profile.min.css
Where
Used on 4 pages

brand-profile-avirahi.html brand-profile-godrej-properties.html people-search.html people.html

Guidelines
Status is inline: the card itself is in dist/brand-profile.min.css, but the rail sizing (.bpr-carousel > .rail > * widths, 3 then 2 then 72vw) the flex track that overrides the grid .bpr-team in dist (a grouped rule .bpr-recog-grid, .bpr-team, .bpr-work-grid, .bpr-spot-group__grid, trimmed here to .bpr-team) and the paginator placement live only in each tenant style block; the @style is that CSS from brand-profile-godrej-properties.html (avirahi is identical, the developer template differs). Without it the cards collapse to their content width. Shipped on godrej-properties (portraits, inline background-image) and avirahi (monograms, inline style); no other tenant has a .bpr-person team. Drift: the design system documents a class-based monogram (.bpr-person__media--mono with .bpr-person__mono), which people.html and people-search.html use (see directory-person-card), but the brand tenants never adopted it and repeat a long inline style per card instead; teearch carries the class CSS with no card using it. _dev/templates/brand-profile-developer.html still renders monograms for people whose portraits the live godrej-properties page now shows.

}

Use it when

  • Leadership of a developer or product brand (the developer family). Real people only, each with a /people/{slug} page
  • Portrait card when a real, verified portrait exists: 4:3 crop, head in the upper third (background-position center 20%)
  • Monogram card when no portrait is on file: the person's initials in Gazpacho on var(--brand)

Avoid

  • Stock, AI-generated or illustrated faces. Real portrait or monogram tile, nothing else
  • Listing people who have no /people profile or no verified role
  • Service-family tenants with two or three partners. They use the compact inline team inside the About card (.bpr-about__team) instead
  • Building a new tenant by pasting this section. A brand starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-developer.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.bpr-team.railclassThe card track, inside .bpr-carousel.rail-outer. The portal carousel script adds drag and paging on the page; without it the track simply scrolls.
.dc-paginator / .dc-page-btn--prev / --nextclassPrev and next buttons in the title row. The --prev and --next modifiers are hooks: an inline page script finds .dc-paginator next to each rail and hands the buttons to initCarousel (see carousel-init). They hide while the rail does not overflow.
.bpr-personclassCard. .bpr-person__link wraps media and body; .bpr-person__foot sits outside the link so Connect is its own target.
.bpr-person__mediaclass4:3 media box painted with --media-placeholder until the image arrives. Portrait: inline background-image. Monogram: inline brand background with Gazpacho initials.
.bpr-person__name / __role / __locationclassName (h3), role with company, and city with a pin icon.
.bpr-person__tagsclassUp to three expertise tags.
.bpr-person__ctaclassConnect button. data-brand-contact opens the contact modal; data-brand carries the person's name.
--brandtokenMonogram tile ground. Set on main.bpr-page by the tenant.

Brand profile tenant theming tokens

Paste In shared CSS

The small set of CSS custom properties and body attributes that theme a brand profile for one tenant: the brand accent and its soft wash, a dark drawing ink, the neutral ink scale, and the page switches for format and dark theme. Everything visual that differs between tenants should come from these.

Needs/dist/styles.min.css/dist/brand-profile.min.css
Where
Used on 9 pages

brand-profile-asian-paints.html brand-profile-avirahi.html brand-profile-godrej-properties.html brand-profile-horizon-architects.html brand-profile-obeetee.html brand-profile-saint-gobain.html brand-profile-scarlet-splendour.html brand-profile-studiofov.html brand-profile-teearch.html

Guidelines
Verified by grep and in the browser against dist on 2026-09-15. --hero-surface and --hero-ink do nothing: setting them changes no pixel, because every tenant's inline hero CSS hardcodes .bpr-hero { background: #1a1714; color: #fff } after dist at the same specificity. --brand-soft, --brand-ink and --warm-white are never read by brand-profile.min.css, only by styles.min.css. Drift: teearch sets --brand-soft #f5e4cf in :root but #f0e6d6 inline on main (main wins inside the page, the chrome outside main gets the other); asian-paints, obeetee, saint-gobain and scarlet-splendour set tokens only in :root, the other five repeat them on main. The template service :root also carries --page, --ink-mute and --ink-strong, which no shared stylesheet reads.
Preview 
<body data-brand-format="atelier">
  <!-- topbar, share sheet and sticky bar sit outside main and keep portal-neutral tokens -->
  <main class="bpr-page" id="main"
        data-brand-slug="brand-slug"
        data-brand-name="Brand Name"
        data-graphics="brand-slug"
        style="--brand:#d5613a; --brand-soft:#f5e4cf;">
    <!-- sections -->
  </main>
</body>

Use it when

  • Set --brand and --brand-soft (and --brand-ink when the tenant has line drawings) in the tenant :root and repeat them inline on main.bpr-page, as the templates do
  • Sample --brand from the real logo file, then derive --brand-soft as a light wash of the same hue
  • body data-brand-format="atelier" on every brand profile; add data-theme="dark" only for a dark tenant
  • Contact card tokens (--contact-*) are their own contract; see brand-profile-contact

Avoid

  • Setting tokens on body or html for a dark tenant. Dark overrides belong on main.bpr-page only, so the topbar, sticky bar, menu and modals keep portal-neutral values
  • Using --brand as a wash behind the hero or on the logo tile. It is for small accents: CTA hover, contact title rule, reach icons, badges
  • Re-theming by writing page CSS against .bpr-* classes. dist/brand-profile.min.css uses body .bpr-* selectors that beat page rules; change a token instead
  • Relying on --hero-surface or --hero-ink (see notes)
  • Hand-building a tenant. A new brand starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-{family}.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile

API

NameTypeWhat it does
--brandtokenTenant accent hex, sampled from the logo. Read by 13 rules in brand-profile.min.css (topbar CTA hover, contact title rule, contact CTA and reach icons) and about 70 in styles.min.css. No CSS default: unset, the contact CTA falls back to var(--ink). The templates ship #d5613a as a placeholder value.
--brand-softtokenLight wash of the accent for chips, monogram grounds and fills. Read only by styles.min.css (about 80 uses). Template placeholder #f5e4cf.
--brand-inktokenDark drawing ink for architectural SVGs and the person contact card gradient. Formula for new tenants: color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand) 55%, #1a1714 45%). Set by 4 tenants.
--ink / --ink2 / --muted / --ruletokenPortal neutrals (#111111, #374151, #6a6a6a, #e8e8e8). A dark tenant swaps them on main.bpr-page.
--warm-whitetokenWarm page ground used by section and card fallbacks in styles.min.css.
--media-placeholdertokenGround painted behind loading media in .bpr-person__media, .bpr-work__media, .bpr-mcard__media and the title card. Default #f0ebe0. No tenant sets it.
--titlecard-meta-color / --titlecard-dividertokenMeta text and rule on title-as-visual media cards. Defaults var(--muted) and a 12% ink mix.
--hero-tooltip-bg / --hero-tooltip-fgtokenHover label on the hero social pills. Defaults #1a1410 and #fff.
--hero-surface / --hero-inktokenDocumented hero ground and text colour, read by the plain .bpr-hero rule in dist. Inert in practice (see notes).
body[data-brand-format]attributeatelier on every tenant. Scopes the shared profile chrome in styles.min.css (sticky bar, share, topbar).
body[data-theme="dark"]attributeDark tenant switch (Studio FOV only today).
main.bpr-page[data-brand-slug][data-brand-name]attributeTenant identity the share and contact scripts read; data-graphics names the brand-graphics asset slug.

Brand profile work rail and project lightbox

Paste Inline CSS: paste it too

The projects or gallery section of a brand profile: a rail of image tiles with a locality eyebrow and project title. Each tile opens a Fancybox lightbox whose side panel (caption below on phones) shows an index, the eyebrow, the title and the project write-up taken from the tile's hidden rich text.

Guidelines
Status is inline: the tile and caption classes exist in dist/brand-profile.min.css, but every tenant repeats about 8 KB of the same work, Fancybox and rail CSS in its style block, and the binding script in @js is inline per page. The @style is teearch's copy with the grouped track rule (.bpr-recog-grid, .bpr-team, .bpr-work-grid, .bpr-spot-group__grid, .bpr-founders__list) trimmed to .bpr-work-grid. Stale comments on every tenant still say PhotoSwipe, and tiles still ship data-pswp-width and data-pswp-height, which the script strips at runtime. The .fb-* classes are this caption, not a feedback component.

(function () {
  var workSection = document.getElementById('work');
  if (!workSection) return;
  var links = workSection.querySelectorAll('a.bpr-work');
  if (!links.length) return;
  var pad2 = function (n) { return n < 10 ? '0' + n : String(n); };
  var total = links.length;
  links.forEach(function (a, i) {
    a.setAttribute('data-fancybox', 'work');
    a.removeAttribute('data-pswp-width');
    a.removeAttribute('data-pswp-height');
    var eye   = a.querySelector('.bpr-work__eye');
    var title = a.querySelector('.bpr-work__title');
    var body  = a.querySelector('.bpr-work__wysiwyg');
    var idxHTML = '<div class="fb-work-idx"><b>' + pad2(i + 1) + '</b><span>/ ' + pad2(total) + '</span></div>';
    var captionHTML = (
      idxHTML +
      (eye   ? '<div class="fb-work-eye">'  + eye.innerHTML   + '</div>' : '') +
      (title ? '<h3 class="fb-work-title">' + title.innerHTML + '</h3>'  : '') +
      '<div class="fb-work-rule"></div>' +
      (body  ? '<div class="fb-work-body">' + body.innerHTML  + '</div>' : '')
    );
    a.setAttribute('data-caption', captionHTML);
  });
  function bindWork() {
    if (typeof window.Fancybox === 'undefined') return false;
    var isMobile = window.matchMedia('(max-width: 767px)').matches;
    var SidebarPlugin = (!isMobile && window.Sidebar) || null;
    var workOpts = {
      plugins: SidebarPlugin ? { Sidebar: SidebarPlugin } : {},
      Sidebar: SidebarPlugin ? { showOnStart: true } : undefined,
      mainStyle: SidebarPlugin ? {
        '--sidebar-width': 'clamp(320px, 30vw, 420px)',
        '--sidebar-padding': '0',
      } : undefined,
      on: isMobile ? {
        'Carousel.change': function (fancybox) {
          var container = fancybox.getContainer && fancybox.getContainer();
          if (container) {
            container.classList.remove('caption-hidden');
            container.classList.remove('has-zoomed');
          }
        },
      } : undefined,
    };
    if (window.gtFancybox && window.gtFancybox.mergeDefaults) {
      workOpts = window.gtFancybox.mergeDefaults(workOpts);
    }
    window.Fancybox.bind('[data-fancybox="work"]', workOpts);
    return true;
  }
  if (!bindWork()) {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', bindWork);
  }
})();

Use it when

  • Signature projects, collections or product lines on any brand tenant, with the brand's real photography
  • The write-up is authored once, in .bpr-work__wysiwyg inside the tile. The page script copies it into the lightbox caption, so the backend never writes caption HTML twice
  • Titles and figures come from the brand's own site or client document

Avoid

  • Invented projects, renders passed off as photos, or unverified areas and counts
  • Opening a separate project modal. #brWorkModal (.bwm-*) is dead scaffolding; the lightbox is the only detail view
  • Hover transforms on the whole anchor. Only the image zooms inside .bpr-work__media
  • Building a new tenant by pasting this section. A brand starts from _dev/templates/brand-profile-{family}.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile

NameTypeWhat it does

.bpr-workclassTile anchor. href is the full-size image. The page script adds data-fancybox="work" and data-caption.
.bpr-work__mediaclassImage figure; painted with --media-placeholder until the image loads.
.bpr-work__eye / .bpr-work__titleclassLocality and type line, and the project name (h3).
.bpr-work__wysiwygclassRich text write-up, hidden on the tile and reused as the lightbox caption body.

Profile mobile sticky contact bar

Paste In shared CSS

The bar pinned to the bottom of a brand or person profile on phones: a Back disc, a full-width Contact button and a Menu disc that opens the portal off-canvas menu. The markup also carries a Share disc, which shared CSS currently hides. It keeps the one action a visitor came for a thumb away at any scroll depth, and stands down while the on-page contact card is in view.

Use it when

  • Every brand profile and person profile, placed after </main>. It shows only at 767px and below; the topbar carries the same actions on wider screens
  • Brand pages: Back goes to /brands and the button reads Contact. Person pages: Back goes to /people and the button reads Get in touch

Avoid

  • Collapsing it to a single button. Back and Menu are the only way back to the directory and into the portal on mobile once the hero is gone
  • Hiding it with page CSS on scroll. The only stand-down is body[data-contact-in-view], set by the contact IntersectionObserver in the page script
  • Letting a dark tenant's tokens reach it. It renders outside main.bpr-page on purpose; tenant --ink overrides must stay scoped to main.bpr-page or the Back disc turns cream on cream
  • Pasting it into a new tenant. Brand tenants start from _dev/templates/brand-profile-{family}.html via the brand-profile-work skill or /new-brand-profile, and person pages come from npm run build:people

API

NameTypeWhat it does
.bpr-sticky-contactclassFixed bottom bar, display:none above 767px.
.bpr-sticky-contact__backclass40px outlined disc linking to the directory.
.bpr-sticky-contact__primaryclassFlex-1 contact button, co-classed .bpr-btn .bpr-btn--light on brands (.pp-btn .pp-btn--primary on people). Carries data-brand-contact. Drops its arrow under 340px.
.bpr-sticky-contact__utilclass40px Share disc carrying data-brand-share. Still in every tenant's markup, but styles.min.css sets body:is(.pp-page, [data-brand-format]) .bpr-sticky-contact__util{display:none!important}, so it never shows. Keep it for parity; do not restyle it back without a decision.
.bpr-sticky-contact__menuclass40px Menu disc; calls openOC() to open the shared #ocMenu. Present on all 9 brand tenants and the person pages.
body[data-brand-format]attributePage context the shared rules are scoped to (body:is(.pp-page, [data-brand-format])). Without it, or body.pp-page, the bar is unstyled. data-theme="dark" on the same body gives it the dark glass treatment.
body[data-contact-in-view]attributeSet by the page while #contact is on screen; slides the bar away.
